cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A fluid is anything that flows: liquids and gases. It cannot keep its own shape.

why.en: Its particles slide past each other easily, so it takes the shape of its container.

example.en: Water takes the shape of a glass. Air fills a tyre.

recall_q.en: What is a fluid?

recall_a.en: A substance that flows — liquid or gas.

explain_simple.en: If it can be poured or it spreads out, it is a fluid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Density (mass density) is mass per unit volume. Density = Mass / Volume. Unit: kg/m³. Symbol: ρ (rho).

why.en: It tells how much 'stuff' is packed into a space.

example.en: Water is 1000 kg/m³. Petrol is lighter, about 750 kg/m³, so petrol floats on water.

recall_q.en: Density of water in kg/m³?

explain_simple.en: Heavy for its size = high density.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific weight (weight density) is weight per unit volume. w = ρ × g. Unit: N/m³.

why.en: Weight is mass pulled by gravity, so multiply density by g (9.81 m/s²).

recall_q.en: Formula for specific weight?

explain_simple.en: Density talks about mass. Specific weight talks about weight.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific volume is volume per unit mass. It is 1 / density. Unit: m³/kg.

why.en: It is just density turned upside down.

recall_q.en: Specific volume is the reciprocal of what?

explain_simple.en: How much space one kilogram takes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific gravity (relative density) = density of the liquid / density of water. It has no unit.

why.en: It compares a liquid with water, so the units cancel.

example.en: Mercury has specific gravity 13.6 — it is 13.6 times heavier than water.

recall_q.en: Specific gravity of mercury?

explain_simple.en: How many times heavier than water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Viscosity is a fluid's resistance to flow — its inner friction. Thick fluid = high viscosity.

why.en: Layers of the fluid rub against each other when they move.

example.en: Honey and engine oil flow slowly. Water and petrol flow fast.

recall_q.en: What is viscosity?

recall_a.en: Resistance to flow (internal friction of a fluid).

explain_simple.en: Viscosity means thickness of a liquid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dynamic viscosity (μ) unit: N·s/m² or Pa·s. CGS unit: poise. 1 poise = 0.1 N·s/m².

why.en: It is shear stress divided by velocity gradient.

recall_q.en: CGS unit of dynamic viscosity?

explain_simple.en: Viscosity is measured in poise or Pa·s.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Kinematic viscosity (ν) = dynamic viscosity / density. SI unit: m²/s. CGS unit: stoke.

why.en: Dividing by density removes the mass part; only length and time remain.

example.en: 1 stoke = 1 cm²/s = 10⁻⁴ m²/s.

recall_q.en: Unit of kinematic viscosity in CGS?

explain_simple.en: Kinematic viscosity = μ / ρ.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Newton's law of viscosity: shear stress is proportional to velocity gradient. τ = μ × (du/dy).

why.en: The faster one layer slides over the next, the more force is needed.

example.en: Stirring honey fast needs more effort than stirring slowly.

recall_q.en: State Newton's law of viscosity as a formula.

explain_simple.en: Faster sliding of layers → more drag.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Viscosity of liquids falls when heated. Viscosity of gases rises when heated.

why.en: In liquids, heat weakens the pull between molecules. In gases, heat makes molecules collide more.

example.en: Cold engine oil is thick in the morning; warm oil is thin.

recall_q.en: What happens to the viscosity of a liquid when it is heated?

explain_simple.en: Hot oil = thin oil. Hot gas = thicker gas.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compressibility is how much a fluid's volume shrinks under pressure. It is 1 / bulk modulus.

why.en: Gases squeeze easily; liquids hardly squeeze at all.

example.en: You can pump much air into a tyre. You cannot squeeze water into a bottle that is full.

recall_q.en: Compressibility is the reciprocal of what?

explain_simple.en: Easy to squeeze = high compressibility.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Surface tension is the pull on a liquid surface that makes it act like a stretched skin. Unit: N/m.

why.en: Molecules on the surface are pulled inward by the molecules below.

example.en: Water drops are round. A small insect can walk on water.

recall_q.en: Unit of surface tension?

explain_simple.en: The surface of water behaves like a thin rubber sheet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Capillarity: a liquid rises or falls in a thin tube. Water rises (wets glass). Mercury falls (does not wet glass).

why.en: It is caused by surface tension and the attraction between the liquid and the tube wall.

example.en: Kerosene climbs up the wick of a lamp.

recall_q.en: In a thin glass tube, does mercury rise or fall?

explain_simple.en: Water climbs a thin tube; mercury goes down.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Capillary rise h = 4σcosθ / (ρgd). Thinner tube → higher rise.

why.en: The diameter d is in the bottom of the formula.

recall_q.en: If the tube is made thinner, what happens to capillary rise?

explain_simple.en: Smaller tube, taller rise.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Specific weight = ρg; specific gravity has no unit.
Viscosity = resistance to flow; τ = μ du/dy.
Surface tension N/m; water rises, mercury falls in a tube.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure = Force / Area. Unit: pascal (Pa) = 1 N/m². 1 bar = 10⁵ Pa.

why.en: The same force on a small area pushes harder.

example.en: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one.

recall_q.en: 1 bar equals how many pascal?

explain_simple.en: Pressure is push on each square metre.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure in a liquid at depth h is p = ρgh. Pressure head h = p / (ρg).

why.en: Deeper down, more liquid sits on top and presses down.

example.en: Ears hurt at the bottom of a deep pond.

recall_q.en: Formula for pressure at depth h in a liquid?

explain_simple.en: Deeper = more pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Absolute pressure = Atmospheric pressure + Gauge pressure.

why.en: A gauge reads zero at normal air pressure, so it misses the air's share.

example.en: A tyre gauge shows 30 psi; real (absolute) pressure is about 30 + 14.7 psi.

recall_q.en: Absolute pressure = ?

explain_simple.en: Real pressure = air pressure + what the gauge shows.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vacuum pressure is pressure below atmospheric. Absolute = Atmospheric − Vacuum.

why.en: Vacuum is how much less than air pressure there is.

example.en: The inlet manifold of a running petrol engine has vacuum.

recall_q.en: Absolute pressure when there is vacuum = ?

explain_simple.en: Vacuum is 'less than air pressure'.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Standard atmospheric pressure = 101.325 kN/m² = 760 mm of mercury = 10.3 m of water.

why.en: The weight of the air above us presses on everything.

recall_q.en: Atmospheric pressure in mm of mercury?

explain_simple.en: Air pressure holds up 760 mm of mercury.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pascal's law: pressure applied on a confined fluid is passed equally in all directions.

why.en: A fluid at rest cannot hold different pressures at the same level.

example.en: Hydraulic brakes, hydraulic jack and hydraulic press work on Pascal's law.

recall_q.en: Hydraulic brakes work on which law?

explain_simple.en: Push the fluid at one end; the push reaches every side equally.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Pressure = F/A, unit Pa; 1 bar = 10⁵ Pa.
Pascal's law → hydraulic brake, jack, press.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A piezometer is a simple open glass tube fixed to a pipe. Liquid rises in it to show pressure.

why.en: Height of liquid in the tube = pressure head.

recall_q.en: Can a piezometer measure vacuum (negative) pressure?

recall_a.en: No. Only small positive pressures of liquids.

explain_simple.en: A straight tube where water climbs to show pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A U-tube manometer has a liquid (often mercury) in a U-shaped tube. It measures high or negative pressure.

why.en: Heavy mercury balances high pressure in a short tube.

recall_q.en: Which instrument measures pressure at one point, including vacuum: piezometer or U-tube manometer?

explain_simple.en: Two arms of a U; the level difference shows pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A differential manometer measures the pressure difference between two points or two pipes.

why.en: Each arm is connected to a different point; the level gap shows the difference.

recall_q.en: What does a differential manometer measure?

explain_simple.en: It compares two pressures.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A Bourdon tube pressure gauge has a bent oval tube that straightens under pressure and turns a pointer.

why.en: Pressure inside a curved tube tries to make it straight.

example.en: Air pressure gauges at petrol pumps and on air-brake trucks.

recall_q.en: What part moves inside a Bourdon gauge?

explain_simple.en: Pressure straightens a bent tube, and the pointer moves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure. A manometer measures fluid pressure in pipes or vessels.

why.en: Different jobs: one reads the air, one reads a system.

recall_q.en: Instrument that measures atmospheric pressure?

explain_simple.en: Baro = air pressure. Mano = pipe pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Piezometer: open tube, low positive pressure only.
U-tube manometer: high and vacuum pressure.
Differential manometer: difference between two points.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ideal fluid: no viscosity and cannot be compressed. It does not exist in real life.

why.en: It is an imaginary fluid used to make calculations easy.

recall_q.en: Does an ideal fluid have viscosity?

explain_simple.en: A perfect, friction-free fluid that exists only on paper.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Real fluid: has viscosity. All actual fluids are real fluids.

why.en: Every real liquid and gas has some inner friction.

example.en: Water, air, oil, petrol.

recall_q.en: A fluid that has viscosity is called?

explain_simple.en: Every fluid you can touch is a real fluid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Newtonian fluid obeys Newton's law of viscosity: viscosity stays the same however fast you stir.

why.en: Shear stress and velocity gradient form a straight line.

example.en: Water, air, petrol, thin oils.

recall_q.en: Is water Newtonian or non-Newtonian?

explain_simple.en: Stir slow or fast — thickness stays the same.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Non-Newtonian fluid does not obey Newton's law: its thickness changes when stirred or pushed.

why.en: Shear stress and velocity gradient do not form a straight line.

example.en: Grease, toothpaste, paint, blood, ketchup.

recall_q.en: Give one example of a non-Newtonian fluid.

explain_simple.en: Its thickness changes when you push it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steady flow: speed and pressure at a point do not change with time. Unsteady flow: they change with time.

why.en: We watch one fixed point and see if things change over time.

example.en: Steady: a tap kept open the same. Unsteady: a tap being opened or closed.

recall_q.en: Flow where conditions at a point do not change with time?

explain_simple.en: Steady = same over time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Uniform flow: velocity is the same at every point along the flow. Non-uniform: velocity changes from point to point.

why.en: Here we compare places, not times.

example.en: Uniform: water in a long straight pipe of same size. Non-uniform: a pipe that narrows.

recall_q.en: Velocity changes from place to place — which flow?

explain_simple.en: Uniform = same everywhere along the pipe.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Laminar flow: fluid moves in smooth parallel layers. Turbulent flow: fluid moves in a mixed, swirling way.

why.en: Slow, thick flow stays orderly; fast flow breaks into whirls.

example.en: Honey poured slowly is laminar. A river in flood is turbulent.

recall_q.en: Flow in smooth parallel layers is called?

explain_simple.en: Laminar = neat layers. Turbulent = messy swirls.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Reynolds number decides the flow type in a pipe: below 2000 laminar, 2000–4000 transition, above 4000 turbulent.

why.en: Re = ρVD/μ compares inertia force with viscous force.

recall_q.en: Reynolds number above which pipe flow is turbulent?

explain_simple.en: Small Re = calm flow. Big Re = rough flow.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Continuity equation: A₁V₁ = A₂V₂. Discharge stays the same through a pipe.

why.en: Liquid cannot vanish or pile up, so what goes in must come out.

example.en: Pinch a garden hose and the water comes out faster.

recall_q.en: Write the continuity equation.

explain_simple.en: Narrow pipe = faster water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Discharge (Q) = Area × Velocity. Unit: m³/s.

why.en: It is the volume that passes each second.

recall_q.en: Unit of discharge?

explain_simple.en: How many cubic metres of water flow each second.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bernoulli's equation: pressure head + velocity head + datum head = constant, for an ideal flowing fluid.

why.en: Energy is not lost; it only changes form.

example.en: Where water speeds up in a narrow pipe, its pressure falls.

recall_q.en: In a narrow part of a pipe, velocity rises. What happens to pressure?

explain_simple.en: Fast fluid = low pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A venturimeter measures discharge in a pipe. It has a converging part, a throat and a diverging part.

why.en: Flow speeds up at the throat; the pressure drop there tells the flow rate (Bernoulli).

example.en: The carburettor venturi uses the same idea to suck petrol.

recall_q.en: What does a venturimeter measure?

recall_a.en: Rate of flow (discharge) in a pipe.

explain_simple.en: A pipe with a waist; the pressure drop at the waist shows the flow.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An orifice is a small opening in the side or bottom of a tank. It is used to measure discharge.

why.en: Velocity through it is about √(2gh), where h is the water height above it.

recall_q.en: Velocity of water from an orifice under head h (ideal)?

explain_simple.en: A hole in a tank; higher water level, faster jet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vena contracta is the narrowest part of a jet just after it leaves an orifice.

why.en: Water streams curve inward as they leave the hole.

recall_q.en: The narrowest section of a jet after an orifice is called?

explain_simple.en: The jet gets thinnest just outside the hole.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coefficient of discharge Cd = Cc × Cv. For an orifice, Cd is about 0.62.

why.en: Real flow is less than ideal because of contraction (Cc) and friction (Cv).

recall_q.en: Cd in terms of Cc and Cv?

explain_simple.en: Real flow ÷ ideal flow.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A notch is an opening at the top of a tank or channel wall, with the water surface below its top. Used to measure flow in open channels.

why.en: The water height over the notch tells the discharge.

example.en: Rectangular, triangular (V-notch) and trapezoidal notches. V-notch is best for small flows.

recall_q.en: Which notch is best for measuring small discharges?

explain_simple.en: A cut in a channel wall that measures flowing water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Major loss in a pipe is loss of head due to friction along its length.

why.en: Fluid rubs against the pipe wall all along the way.

recall_q.en: Loss of head due to pipe friction is called?

explain_simple.en: Long pipe = big friction loss.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Minor losses come from bends, valves, sudden enlargement, sudden contraction, pipe entry and exit.

why.en: The flow is disturbed and swirls at each fitting.

recall_q.en: Name two causes of minor loss.

recall_a.en: Bends, valves, sudden enlargement/contraction, entry, exit.

explain_simple.en: Every bend or fitting wastes a little energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Darcy–Weisbach formula: hf = 4fLV² / (2gD). Loss grows with pipe length and with velocity squared.

why.en: Longer pipe and faster flow mean more rubbing.

recall_q.en: Darcy's formula for head loss due to friction?

explain_simple.en: Double the speed → four times the loss.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Chezy's formula: V = C √(m i). m = hydraulic mean depth, i = slope (loss of head per unit length).

why.en: Used for flow in pipes and open channels.

recall_q.en: In Chezy's formula V = C√(mi), what is m?

explain_simple.en: Chezy gives speed from slope and depth.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic mean depth m = Area / wetted perimeter. For a full circular pipe, m = D/4.

why.en: πD²/4 divided by πD gives D/4.

recall_q.en: Hydraulic mean depth of a full pipe?

explain_simple.en: Pipe diameter divided by four.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Viscosity index (VI) shows how little an oil's viscosity changes with temperature. High VI = good oil.

why.en: A good oil should not get too thin when hot or too thick when cold.

example.en: Multigrade engine oils like 20W-40 have high VI.

recall_q.en: Is a high or low viscosity index better?

explain_simple.en: High VI = oil thickness stays steady in heat and cold.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oxidation stability is an oil's ability to resist reacting with oxygen and forming sludge and acids.

why.en: Hot oil plus air slowly turns into gum and varnish.

recall_q.en: Resistance of oil to sludge and acid formation by air is called?

explain_simple.en: Good oil does not 'rot' when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Demulsibility is an oil's ability to separate from water quickly.

why.en: Water mixed into oil (emulsion) causes rust and poor lubrication.

recall_q.en: Ability of oil to separate from water is called?

explain_simple.en: Good oil lets water fall out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lubricity (oiliness) is an oil's ability to reduce friction and wear between surfaces.

why.en: It forms a thin slippery film on metal.

recall_q.en: Ability of oil to reduce friction and wear?

explain_simple.en: How slippery the oil is.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rust prevention: hydraulic oil must protect steel parts from rusting, using added inhibitors.

why.en: Moisture enters hydraulic systems and attacks metal.

recall_q.en: Why are rust inhibitors added to hydraulic oil?

recall_a.en: To protect metal parts from rust.

explain_simple.en: Oil coats metal so water cannot rust it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pour point is the lowest temperature at which an oil will still flow.

why.en: Below it, wax in the oil sets and the oil stops pouring.

example.en: Important for vehicles in cold hill areas like Munnar.

recall_q.en: Lowest temperature at which oil flows is?

explain_simple.en: Colder than pour point, the oil will not pour.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Flash point: lowest temperature at which oil vapour flashes briefly near a flame. Fire point: lowest temperature at which it keeps burning (at least 5 s). Fire point is higher.

why.en: First a quick flash, then, a little hotter, steady burning.

recall_q.en: Which is higher: flash point or fire point?

explain_simple.en: Flash first, fire later.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Neutralisation number shows how acidic or basic an oil is. Rising acid number means the oil is getting old.

why.en: Oxidation makes acids that attack metal.

recall_q.en: What does the neutralisation number of oil indicate?

explain_simple.en: An 'acid level' test for oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Oxidation stability = no sludge; demulsibility = separates from water.
Lubricity = slipperiness; rust inhibitors protect steel.
Flash point < fire point; neutralisation no. = acidity.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A pump turns mechanical energy into hydraulic (pressure) energy. A turbine turns hydraulic energy into mechanical energy.

why.en: They do opposite jobs.

example.en: A water pump fills a tank. A turbine at Idukki dam makes power.

recall_q.en: Which machine changes hydraulic energy to mechanical energy?

explain_simple.en: Pump pushes water. Turbine is pushed by water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A centrifugal pump spins an impeller. The spinning throws water outward, building pressure. It is a rotodynamic pump.

why.en: Centrifugal force pushes water from the centre to the rim.

example.en: Most house water pumps and engine coolant pumps.

recall_q.en: The rotating part of a centrifugal pump is called?

explain_simple.en: A spinning wheel flings water out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A centrifugal pump must be primed (filled with liquid) before starting.

why.en: An impeller spinning in air cannot create enough suction.

recall_q.en: What is priming?

recall_a.en: Filling the pump and suction pipe with liquid before starting.

explain_simple.en: Fill it with water first, or it will not pick up water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A reciprocating pump uses a piston moving to and fro inside a cylinder. It is a positive displacement pump.

why.en: Each stroke pushes out a fixed volume.

example.en: Hand pumps and high-pressure washer pumps.

recall_q.en: Is a reciprocating pump rotodynamic or positive displacement?

explain_simple.en: A piston sucks in and pushes out water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Slip = theoretical discharge − actual discharge. % slip = (Qth − Qact)/Qth × 100.

why.en: Some liquid leaks back past valves and the piston.

recall_q.en: Formula for slip of a reciprocating pump?

explain_simple.en: Water that should come out but leaks back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Negative slip happens when actual discharge is more than theoretical. It occurs with long suction pipe, short delivery pipe and high speed.

why.en: Water keeps moving by its own momentum and the delivery valve opens early.

recall_q.en: When is slip of a reciprocating pump negative?

explain_simple.en: More water comes out than the piston pushed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Theoretical discharge of a single-acting reciprocating pump: Q = A L N / 60. Double acting: Q = 2 A L N / 60.

why.en: Double acting pushes water on both sides of the piston.

recall_q.en: Discharge of a double-acting reciprocating pump?

explain_simple.en: Double acting gives twice the water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An air vessel on a reciprocating pump gives a steady flow and saves power.

why.en: It stores and releases water like a cushion, smoothing the pulses.

recall_q.en: Purpose of an air vessel in a reciprocating pump?

recall_a.en: Steady flow and saving power (less friction).

explain_simple.en: A shock-absorber for water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific speed of a pump: Ns = N√Q / H^(3/4). Of a turbine: Ns = N√P / H^(5/4).

why.en: It compares machines of different sizes on one scale.

recall_q.en: Specific speed formula of a turbine?

explain_simple.en: A single number that tells which type of machine suits a job.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Impulse turbine: water hits buckets as a high-speed jet at atmospheric pressure. Example: Pelton wheel. Used for high head.

why.en: All pressure is changed to speed in the nozzle before hitting the wheel.

recall_q.en: Pelton wheel is which type of turbine?

explain_simple.en: A jet of water hits cups on a wheel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Reaction turbine: water enters under pressure and both pressure and speed drop inside the runner. Examples: Francis (medium head), Kaplan (low head).

why.en: The runner is pushed by the reaction of water leaving it.

recall_q.en: Kaplan turbine is used for what head?

explain_simple.en: Water fills the turbine and pushes as it leaves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A draft tube is used in reaction turbines, not in impulse turbines. It recovers energy at the outlet.

why.en: It lets water leave slowly, gaining back some head.

recall_q.en: Is a draft tube used in a Pelton wheel?

explain_simple.en: Reaction turbines have a draft tube; Pelton does not.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Pump: mechanical → hydraulic. Turbine: hydraulic → mechanical.
Reciprocating pump: piston, slip = Qth − Qact, air vessel.
Francis (medium), Kaplan (low head) = reaction, draft tube.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A liquid has a fixed volume but no fixed shape. A gas has neither a fixed volume nor a fixed shape.

why.en: Gas molecules are far apart and spread to fill any space.

example.en: One litre of milk stays one litre in any vessel. LPG gas spreads through a whole room.

recall_q.en: Which has a fixed volume: liquid or gas?

explain_simple.en: Liquid keeps its amount. Gas spreads everywhere.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Density of mercury is 13,600 kg/m³. Density of air at room temperature is about 1.2 kg/m³.

why.en: Mercury is a heavy metal; air is mostly empty space.

recall_q.en: Density of mercury?

explain_simple.en: Mercury is 13.6 times heavier than water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific weight of water = 9.81 kN/m³ (9810 N/m³).

recall_q.en: Specific weight of water in kN/m³?

explain_simple.en: One cubic metre of water weighs about 9.81 kN.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Density of a liquid = specific gravity × 1000 kg/m³.

why.en: Specific gravity tells how many times heavier than water it is.

example.en: Oil with S = 0.8 has density 0.8 × 1000 = 800 kg/m³.

recall_q.en: Density of oil with specific gravity 0.9?

explain_simple.en: Multiply specific gravity by 1000.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dimensions of dynamic viscosity: M L⁻¹ T⁻¹. Dimensions of kinematic viscosity: L² T⁻¹.

why.en: Kinematic viscosity has no mass because density is divided out.

recall_q.en: Dimension of kinematic viscosity?

explain_simple.en: Kinematic viscosity has only length and time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Viscosity of water at 20°C is about 1 centipoise (0.001 Pa·s).

why.en: This is a handy reference value.

recall_q.en: Viscosity of water at 20°C in centipoise?

explain_simple.en: Water ≈ 1 cP.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cohesion is attraction between molecules of the same liquid. Adhesion is attraction between the liquid and another surface.

why.en: These two forces decide whether a liquid wets a surface.

example.en: Water sticks to glass (adhesion stronger). Mercury forms balls (cohesion stronger).

recall_q.en: Attraction between molecules of the same liquid is called?

explain_simple.en: Cohesion = same sticks to same. Adhesion = sticks to others.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Water wets glass because adhesion is more than cohesion. Mercury does not wet glass because cohesion is more.

why.en: The stronger force wins at the contact line.

recall_q.en: Why does mercury not wet glass?

recall_a.en: Its cohesion is greater than adhesion.

explain_simple.en: Mercury likes itself more than it likes glass.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Water's surface in a glass tube curves down in the middle (concave). Mercury's surface curves up (convex).

why.en: Water climbs the wall; mercury pulls away from it.

recall_q.en: Shape of the mercury surface in a glass tube?

explain_simple.en: Water dips; mercury bulges.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Surface tension falls when temperature rises.

why.en: Heat weakens the pull between surface molecules.

example.en: Hot water cleans better partly because it spreads more easily.

recall_q.en: Effect of heating on surface tension?

explain_simple.en: Hotter liquid, weaker skin.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure inside a liquid droplet: p = 4σ/d. Inside a soap bubble: p = 8σ/d.

why.en: A soap bubble has two surfaces (inside and outside), so double.

recall_q.en: Pressure inside a soap bubble of diameter d?

explain_simple.en: Bubble has two skins, so twice the droplet value.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vapour pressure is the pressure of a liquid's vapour above it. It rises with temperature.

why.en: Hotter liquid sends more molecules into the air.

example.en: Petrol has high vapour pressure — it evaporates fast.

recall_q.en: What happens to vapour pressure when temperature rises?

explain_simple.en: Hot liquid gives off more vapour.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cavitation: when local pressure falls below vapour pressure, vapour bubbles form and then collapse violently.

why.en: Collapsing bubbles hammer metal surfaces.

example.en: Pitting on pump impellers, propellers and turbine blades.

recall_q.en: What damage does cavitation cause?

recall_a.en: Pitting and erosion of metal, noise and vibration.

explain_simple.en: Tiny bubbles burst and chip the metal.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bulk modulus K = increase in pressure / volumetric strain. Unit: N/m². Water ≈ 2.1 × 10⁹ N/m².

why.en: It measures how hard a fluid is to squeeze.

recall_q.en: Formula for bulk modulus?

explain_simple.en: Big K = very hard to squeeze.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Liquids are taken as incompressible. Gases are compressible.

why.en: A liquid's volume hardly changes even under large pressure.

example.en: That is why brake fluid can pass pedal force to the wheels.

recall_q.en: Why is brake fluid good for passing force?

explain_simple.en: Liquid does not squash, so it carries the push.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: PSC trap: viscosity measures resistance to flow; viscosity index measures how viscosity changes with temperature.

why.en: Two similar words, two different ideas.

recall_q.en: Which one tells change of thickness with temperature: viscosity or viscosity index?

explain_simple.en: Viscosity = how thick. VI = how steady.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A Redwood or Saybolt viscometer measures oil viscosity by timing how long 50 or 60 ml of oil takes to flow out.

why.en: Thicker oil takes more seconds.

recall_q.en: Name an instrument used to measure oil viscosity.

explain_simple.en: Time how long oil takes to drain — longer = thicker.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gas law for an ideal gas: p v = R T (per kg) or pV = mRT. For air, R = 287 J/kg·K.

why.en: Pressure, volume and temperature of a gas are linked.

recall_q.en: Gas constant R for air?

explain_simple.en: pV = mRT ties together pressure, volume and temperature.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: 1 kgf/cm² ≈ 0.981 bar ≈ 98.1 kPa. Tyre pressure in India is often written in psi; 1 bar ≈ 14.5 psi.

why.en: Gauges use different units; know the conversions.

example.en: A car tyre at 32 psi ≈ 2.2 bar.

recall_q.en: 1 bar is about how many psi?

explain_simple.en: 1 bar ≈ 1 kgf/cm² ≈ 14.5 psi.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure at a point in a fluid at rest is the same in all directions.

why.en: This is the hydrostatic law; a still fluid cannot push more one way than another.

recall_q.en: Is pressure at a point in a still fluid the same in all directions?

explain_simple.en: At one spot, fluid pushes equally every way.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure in a liquid depends only on depth, not on the shape or width of the vessel. This is the hydrostatic paradox.

why.en: p = ρgh has no area in it.

example.en: A narrow pipe and a wide tank of the same depth have the same pressure at the bottom.

recall_q.en: Does the shape of a vessel change the pressure at its bottom?

explain_simple.en: Same depth, same pressure — any shape.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: 10 m of water head ≈ 1 bar ≈ 1 atmosphere.

recall_q.en: About how many metres of water make 1 bar?

explain_simple.en: Every 10 m deeper in water adds about 1 bar.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: To change head of one liquid to another: h₁ × S₁ = h₂ × S₂.

why.en: The same pressure needs a shorter column of a heavier liquid.

recall_q.en: 760 mm of mercury equals about how many metres of water?

explain_simple.en: Heavier liquid, shorter column.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic jack: force multiplication F₂ = F₁ × (A₂/A₁).

why.en: Same pressure acts on both pistons; bigger piston gets bigger force.

example.en: A small push on the jack handle lifts a car.

recall_q.en: In a hydraulic jack, which piston gives the bigger force?

explain_simple.en: Small push on small piston = big push on big piston.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Total pressure (force) on a flat surface under liquid = ρ g A h̄, where h̄ is depth of its centroid.

why.en: Average pressure is at the centre of the area.

recall_q.en: Total pressure on an immersed plane surface?

explain_simple.en: Area × pressure at its centre.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Centre of pressure is the point where the total liquid force acts. On a vertical surface it is always below the centroid.

why.en: Pressure is bigger lower down.

recall_q.en: On a vertical immersed plate, is the centre of pressure above or below the centroid?

explain_simple.en: The push acts lower than the middle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Buoyancy (Archimedes): a body in a fluid feels an upward force equal to the weight of fluid it pushes aside.

why.en: Pressure below the body is more than pressure above it.

example.en: A ship floats; an iron nail sinks.

recall_q.en: Upward force on a body in a fluid equals?

explain_simple.en: Water pushes up as much as the water moved away weighs.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Metacentre: a floating body is stable if the metacentre (M) is above its centre of gravity (G).

why.en: When tilted, buoyancy then turns it back upright.

recall_q.en: Condition for stable equilibrium of a floating body?

explain_simple.en: M above G = boat comes back up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mercury is used in manometers because it is heavy, does not stick to glass, and does not evaporate easily.

why.en: A heavy liquid keeps the tube short for high pressures.

recall_q.en: Give one reason mercury is used in manometers.

recall_a.en: High density (also non-wetting, low vapour pressure).

explain_simple.en: Heavy and clean — short tube, clear reading.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An inverted U-tube differential manometer uses a light liquid (or air) at the top. It measures small pressure differences.

why.en: A light liquid gives a larger, easier-to-read level difference.

recall_q.en: Which manometer measures very small pressure differences between two points?

explain_simple.en: U upside down with light liquid for tiny differences.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A micromanometer (single-column with a large reservoir or inclined tube) measures very small pressures accurately.

why.en: Tilting the tube stretches a small rise into a long reading.

recall_q.en: Why is an inclined tube manometer used?

recall_a.en: To read very small pressures more accurately.

explain_simple.en: A slanted tube makes small changes look bigger.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A Pitot tube measures the velocity of flow at a point. It is an L-shaped tube facing the flow.

why.en: The flow stops at its mouth, and the rise in liquid shows velocity head: V = √(2gh).

example.en: Aircraft speed sensors use Pitot tubes.

recall_q.en: Instrument to measure velocity at a point in a flow?

explain_simple.en: A bent tube facing the flow shows how fast it is moving.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A rotameter measures flow with a float inside a tapered glass tube. Higher flow lifts the float higher.

why.en: More flow needs a wider gap, which is higher up the tapered tube.

recall_q.en: In which instrument does a float rise in a tapered tube?

explain_simple.en: More flow, higher float.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ideal plastic (Bingham) fluid needs a minimum stress before it starts to flow.

why.en: Below that stress it acts like a solid.

example.en: Toothpaste and sewage sludge.

recall_q.en: Toothpaste starts flowing only after a minimum push. What type of fluid?

explain_simple.en: It stays put until you squeeze hard enough.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thixotropic fluids get thinner the longer they are stirred. Example: paint, printer ink.

why.en: Stirring breaks their inner structure.

recall_q.en: Paint gets thinner when stirred for a while. This is called?

explain_simple.en: Stir it longer, it gets thinner.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compressible fluid: density changes with pressure (gases). Incompressible fluid: density stays nearly constant (liquids).

why.en: Gas molecules can be pushed closer; liquid molecules cannot.

recall_q.en: Air in a tyre is compressible or incompressible?

explain_simple.en: Gas squashes, liquid does not.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook
Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compressible flow: density changes along the flow (gases at high speed). Incompressible flow: density stays constant (liquids).

why.en: Fast gas gets squeezed and expanded as it moves.

recall_q.en: Flow of water in a pipe is compressible or incompressible?

explain_simple.en: Water keeps the same density as it flows.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rotational flow: fluid particles spin about their own axis. Irrotational flow: they do not spin.

why.en: Viscosity near walls makes particles rotate.

recall_q.en: Flow in which particles do not rotate about their own axis?

explain_simple.en: Rotational = particles spin. Irrotational = no spin.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: One-dimensional flow: velocity changes in one direction only. Two- and three-dimensional flows change in more directions.

why.en: Engineers simplify pipe flow as one-dimensional.

recall_q.en: Pipe flow is usually treated as how many dimensional?

explain_simple.en: Count the directions in which speed changes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A streamline is an imaginary line that shows the direction of flow at every point. Streamlines never cross.

why.en: A particle cannot move in two directions at once.

recall_q.en: Can two streamlines cross?

explain_simple.en: Flow lines never cut each other.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In Bernoulli's equation the three heads are: pressure head p/ρg, velocity (kinetic) head V²/2g and datum (potential) head z.

why.en: Each is energy per unit weight, measured in metres.

recall_q.en: Velocity head in Bernoulli's equation?

explain_simple.en: Pressure, speed and height — each as metres of fluid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bernoulli's equation assumes: ideal (non-viscous), incompressible, steady flow along a streamline.

why.en: Real flows have losses, so a loss term is added later.

recall_q.en: Name one assumption of Bernoulli's equation.

recall_a.en: Ideal, incompressible, steady flow along a streamline.

explain_simple.en: It works best for smooth, frictionless, steady flow.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic gradient line (HGL) joins pressure + datum heads. Total energy line (TEL) is higher than HGL by V²/2g.

why.en: TEL adds the velocity head on top.

recall_q.en: TEL lies above HGL by how much?

explain_simple.en: Energy line sits above the pressure line by the speed part.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Venturimeter's coefficient of discharge is high, about 0.96–0.98. Orifice meter's is low, about 0.6.

why.en: A venturimeter's smooth shape wastes little energy.

recall_q.en: Which has a higher Cd: venturimeter or orifice meter?

explain_simple.en: Smooth shape → less loss → higher Cd.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In a venturimeter, the converging cone is short and the diverging cone is long (angle about 5–7°).

why.en: A slow, gentle widening stops the flow from breaking away and losing energy.

recall_q.en: Which part of a venturimeter is longer: converging or diverging?

explain_simple.en: Quick narrowing, slow widening.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An orifice meter is a thin plate with a hole fitted in a pipe. It is cheaper but loses more energy than a venturimeter.

why.en: The sudden hole creates swirls.

recall_q.en: Cheaper flow meter with more loss: venturimeter or orifice meter?

explain_simple.en: A plate with a hole: cheap but wasteful.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coefficient of contraction Cc = jet area at vena contracta / orifice area (about 0.64). Coefficient of velocity Cv ≈ 0.97–0.99.

why.en: The jet narrows (Cc) and slows a little by friction (Cv).

recall_q.en: Approximate value of Cc for a sharp orifice?

explain_simple.en: The jet is only about two-thirds the hole size.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A mouthpiece is a short tube (2–3 times its diameter) fitted to an orifice. It increases discharge.

why.en: It reduces jet contraction.

recall_q.en: Effect of fitting a mouthpiece on an orifice?

explain_simple.en: A short pipe on the hole lets more water out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Discharge over a rectangular notch Q ∝ H^(3/2). Over a triangular (V) notch Q ∝ H^(5/2).

why.en: The V shape widens as water rises, so flow grows faster with H.

recall_q.en: Discharge over a V-notch is proportional to H to the power?

explain_simple.en: Rectangle: H^1.5. Triangle: H^2.5.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A weir is a large notch, usually built of masonry across a river or canal. A notch is small and made of metal plate.

why.en: Same idea, different size and material.

recall_q.en: Difference between a notch and a weir?

recall_a.en: Notch: small, metal plate. Weir: large, masonry structure.

explain_simple.en: A weir is a big notch across a river.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Momentum equation: force on a fluid = rate of change of momentum. Used to find force of a jet on a plate.

why.en: Newton's second law applied to flowing fluid.

recall_q.en: Force of a jet on a flat plate comes from which principle?

explain_simple.en: Stopping a water jet needs a force.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: Water flows at 2 m/s in a pipe of area 0.02 m². It enters a pipe of area 0.01 m². Find the new velocity.

explain.en: Same water must pass both pipes each second.
Half the area, double the speed.

summary.en: Half the area → double the speed.

recall_q.en: Area halves. What happens to velocity?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A pipe of area 0.05 m² carries water at 3 m/s. Find discharge.

explain.en: 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

recall_q.en: Formula for discharge?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Loss due to sudden enlargement = (V₁ − V₂)² / 2g.

why.en: Fast water hits slow water and swirls, wasting energy.

recall_q.en: Head loss at sudden enlargement?

explain_simple.en: Loss depends on the drop in speed, squared.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Loss at pipe entrance = 0.5 V²/2g. Loss at pipe exit = V²/2g.

why.en: At exit, all the velocity energy is lost into the tank.

recall_q.en: Head loss at exit of a pipe into a tank?

explain_simple.en: Entry loses half a velocity head; exit loses a full one.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Loss due to sudden contraction ≈ 0.5 V₂²/2g (V₂ = velocity in the smaller pipe).

why.en: The vena contracta forms and then the flow expands again.

recall_q.en: Approximate head loss at sudden contraction?

explain_simple.en: About half the velocity head of the small pipe.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: For laminar flow, friction factor f = 16/Re (or Darcy f' = 64/Re).

why.en: In laminar flow, friction depends only on Reynolds number, not on roughness.

recall_q.en: Darcy friction factor for laminar flow?

explain_simple.en: Laminar flow: friction = 64 divided by Re.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hagen–Poiseuille equation gives head loss in laminar pipe flow: hf = 32 μ V L / (ρ g D²).

why.en: In laminar flow, loss grows directly with velocity (not velocity squared).

recall_q.en: In laminar flow, head loss varies with velocity to which power?

explain_simple.en: Laminar: double speed → double loss.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Moody diagram links friction factor with Reynolds number and pipe roughness for turbulent flow.

why.en: In turbulent flow, roughness also matters.

recall_q.en: Which chart gives friction factor for rough pipes?

explain_simple.en: A chart to look up pipe friction.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Water hammer is a pressure surge when a valve in a pipe is closed suddenly.

why.en: Moving water is stopped quickly, and its momentum turns into a pressure wave.

example.en: A banging noise in house pipes when a tap shuts quickly.

recall_q.en: Pressure rise due to sudden closing of a valve is called?

explain_simple.en: Stopping water fast makes a big pressure knock.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pipes in series: same discharge, head losses add. Pipes in parallel: same head loss, discharges add.

why.en: Like electric circuits: series shares current, parallel shares voltage.

recall_q.en: In pipes in parallel, what is the same in each pipe?

explain_simple.en: Series: same flow. Parallel: same loss.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas

points.en: Major loss = pipe friction, Darcy hf = 4fLV²/2gD.
Minor losses: bends, valves, enlargement, contraction, entry, exit.
Chezy V = C√(mi); m = D/4 for a full pipe.
Laminar f = 64/Re; water hammer = sudden valve closing.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cloud point is the temperature at which wax crystals first make the oil look cloudy. It is a little above the pour point.

why.en: Wax starts separating before the oil fully stops flowing.

recall_q.en: Which is higher: cloud point or pour point?

explain_simple.en: First it looks cloudy, then it stops pouring.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Foam resistance: a good hydraulic oil must not foam. Air bubbles make the system spongy.

why.en: Air compresses, so the hydraulic action becomes soft and slow.

recall_q.en: Why should hydraulic oil resist foaming?

recall_a.en: Air bubbles make the system spongy and weak.

explain_simple.en: Foam = air = soft, weak hydraulics.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Main jobs of a hydraulic oil: pass power, lubricate, seal, cool and protect from rust.

why.en: One liquid does many jobs inside the system.

recall_q.en: Name the main job of a hydraulic fluid.

recall_a.en: To transmit power (also lubricate, seal, cool).

explain_simple.en: It carries the push and keeps parts healthy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: SAE number shows the viscosity grade of engine oil. 'W' means winter grade. In 20W-40, the oil acts like SAE 20 when cold and SAE 40 when hot.

why.en: Multigrade oil works in both cold start and hot running.

recall_q.en: In 20W-40 oil, what does W stand for?

explain_simple.en: First number for cold, second for hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic brake fluid is not mineral oil. It is glycol based (DOT 3, DOT 4).

why.en: Mineral oil swells and ruins the rubber seals of the brake system.

recall_q.en: Is brake fluid a mineral oil?

explain_simple.en: Brake fluid is special; engine oil will damage brake seals.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake fluid absorbs moisture from air (hygroscopic). This lowers its boiling point, so it is changed regularly.

why.en: Boiling fluid makes vapour, and the brake pedal goes soft (vapour lock).

recall_q.en: Why must brake fluid be replaced periodically?

recall_a.en: It absorbs water, which lowers its boiling point.

explain_simple.en: Old brake fluid holds water and can boil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Main parts of a centrifugal pump: impeller, casing, suction pipe with foot valve and strainer, delivery pipe.

why.en: Each part moves water from sump to tank.

recall_q.en: Which part stops water draining back when a centrifugal pump stops?

explain_simple.en: The foot valve keeps the pipe full.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A volute casing is spiral-shaped; its area grows towards the outlet. It turns velocity into pressure.

why.en: Water slows as the passage widens, raising pressure.

recall_q.en: Shape of the casing of a centrifugal pump?

explain_simple.en: A snail-shell casing changes speed into pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Manometric head of a centrifugal pump = actual head the pump develops (static head + losses + exit velocity head).

why.en: The pump must lift water and also overcome pipe losses.

recall_q.en: What is manometric head?

recall_a.en: The total head the pump must develop.

explain_simple.en: Height lifted plus losses.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Manometric efficiency = manometric head / head given by the impeller. Overall efficiency = water power / shaft power.

why.en: Efficiencies show where energy is lost.

recall_q.en: Overall efficiency of a pump?

explain_simple.en: Useful output ÷ input.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pumps in series increase head. Pumps in parallel increase discharge.

why.en: Series: each pump adds lift. Parallel: each pump adds flow.

recall_q.en: To get more head, connect pumps in series or parallel?

explain_simple.en: Series = higher. Parallel = more.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: NPSH (net positive suction head) must be enough at the pump inlet, or cavitation starts.

why.en: Low suction pressure lets water boil into vapour bubbles.

recall_q.en: What happens if available NPSH is too low?

explain_simple.en: Too little suction pressure → bubbles → damage.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A centrifugal pump suits large flow at low or medium head. A reciprocating pump suits small flow at high head.

why.en: Spinning impellers move lots of water; pistons build high pressure.

recall_q.en: Which pump suits high head with small flow?

explain_simple.en: Lots of water → centrifugal. High pressure → reciprocating.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gear pumps and vane pumps are rotary positive displacement pumps. They are used for oil and power steering.

why.en: They trap oil and push a fixed amount each turn.

example.en: The engine oil pump is usually a gear pump.

recall_q.en: Engine oil pumps are commonly which type?

explain_simple.en: Gears trap oil and carry it round.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pelton wheel parts: nozzle with spear, runner with buckets, casing, breaking jet. Buckets have a splitter in the middle.

why.en: The splitter divides the jet into two halves so there is no side thrust.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the splitter in a Pelton bucket?

recall_a.en: To divide the jet into two equal parts (avoid side thrust).

explain_simple.en: The middle ridge splits the jet into two.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Best speed ratio of a Pelton wheel is about 0.46 (bucket speed ≈ half the jet speed).

why.en: Maximum work when bucket speed is half the jet speed.

recall_q.en: Ideal ratio of bucket speed to jet speed in a Pelton wheel?

explain_simple.en: Buckets move at about half the jet speed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Francis turbine is an inward mixed-flow reaction turbine with fixed runner blades and guide vanes.

why.en: Water enters radially and leaves axially.

recall_q.en: Francis turbine flow direction?

explain_simple.en: Water comes in from the sides and leaves down the middle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Kaplan turbine is an axial-flow reaction turbine with adjustable runner blades. A propeller turbine has fixed blades.

why.en: Adjustable blades keep efficiency high when flow changes.

recall_q.en: Which axial turbine has adjustable runner blades?

explain_simple.en: Kaplan = a ship's propeller with blades that turn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific speed ranges: Pelton low (about 10–35), Francis medium (about 60–300), Kaplan high (300–1000).

why.en: Low head machines must spin fast for their size.

recall_q.en: Which turbine has the highest specific speed?

explain_simple.en: Pelton slow, Francis middle, Kaplan fast.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Impulse vs reaction: impulse works at atmospheric pressure, partly filled, no draft tube. Reaction runs full of water under pressure, with a draft tube.

why.en: In impulse turbines all energy is speed; in reaction both pressure and speed act.

recall_q.en: Which turbine runs full of water under pressure?

explain_simple.en: Impulse = jet hits cups. Reaction = water fills and pushes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Governing of a turbine keeps its speed constant when load changes, by controlling the water flow.

why.en: Generators must run at fixed speed to give 50 Hz power.

recall_q.en: Why are turbines governed?

recall_a.en: To keep speed constant as load changes.

explain_simple.en: Less load → less water, so speed stays the same.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A hydraulic ram lifts part of a water flow to a higher level using water hammer. It needs no outside power.

why.en: The pressure surge of stopped water pushes some water up.

recall_q.en: Which device lifts water using water hammer, without a motor?

explain_simple.en: A pump that runs on the knock of stopped water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic accumulator stores hydraulic energy (pressurised liquid) for later use.

why.en: It supplies extra flow when demand is high.

recall_q.en: Device that stores energy as pressurised liquid?

explain_simple.en: A storage tank for hydraulic pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic intensifier increases the pressure of a liquid using a large and a small piston.

why.en: Low pressure on the big piston gives high pressure under the small one.

recall_q.en: Device that raises liquid pressure?

explain_simple.en: Big piston pushes small piston to raise pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Worked example: slip of a reciprocating pump

text.en: Question: Theoretical discharge is 10 litres/s. Actual is 9.5 litres/s. Find percentage slip.

explain.en: Cd and slip add up: 0.95 + 0.05 = 1.

recall_q.en: If Cd = 0.95, what is % slip?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermodynamics is the study of heat, work and energy, and how one changes into another.

why.en: Engines turn heat from fuel into work that moves the vehicle.

recall_q.en: What does thermodynamics study?

explain_simple.en: How heat becomes motion.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A system is the part we study. Everything outside it is the surroundings. The line between them is the boundary.

why.en: We must decide what is 'inside' before counting energy.

example.en: The gas inside an engine cylinder is the system; the piston and walls are the boundary.

recall_q.en: Everything outside a system is called?

explain_simple.en: System = what you watch. Surroundings = the rest.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Closed system: mass does not cross, energy can. Open system: both mass and energy cross. Isolated system: neither crosses.

why.en: Different machines exchange different things.

example.en: Closed: gas in a cylinder with valves shut. Open: a compressor. Isolated: a perfect thermos flask.

recall_q.en: In which system can neither mass nor energy cross?

explain_simple.en: Closed lets heat out, open lets stuff out, isolated lets nothing out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Intensive properties do not depend on mass (pressure, temperature, density). Extensive properties depend on mass (volume, energy, mass).

why.en: Cut a system in half: intensive stays the same, extensive halves.

recall_q.en: Is temperature intensive or extensive?

explain_simple.en: Half a cup of hot tea is still just as hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Heat and work are energy in transit. They are path functions, not properties.

why.en: Their amount depends on how the change happens, not only on start and end.

recall_q.en: Is work a property or a path function?

explain_simple.en: Heat and work depend on the road taken.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Absolute temperature: K = °C + 273.

why.en: Gas laws need temperature from absolute zero.

recall_q.en: 27°C in kelvin?

explain_simple.en: Add 273 to Celsius.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific heat is the heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C. For gases there are two: cp (constant pressure) and cv (constant volume).

why.en: At constant pressure the gas also expands and does work, so cp is bigger.

recall_q.en: Which is greater for a gas: cp or cv?

explain_simple.en: Heating with room to expand needs more heat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: For air: cp = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, cv = 0.718 kJ/kg·K, γ = cp/cv = 1.4, R = cp − cv = 0.287 kJ/kg·K.

why.en: These values are used in every air-cycle problem.

recall_q.en: Value of γ (gamma) for air?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Internal energy is energy stored in a substance due to its molecules' motion. For an ideal gas it depends only on temperature.

why.en: Hotter gas molecules move faster.

recall_q.en: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends on what?

explain_simple.en: Hotter gas holds more energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Enthalpy H = U + pV. It is the total heat content of a flowing fluid.

why.en: Flowing fluid carries both internal energy and pressure energy.

recall_q.en: Formula of enthalpy?

explain_simple.en: Stored energy plus pushing energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Entropy is a measure of disorder. In a reversible adiabatic process entropy stays constant.

why.en: No heat crosses and no friction, so disorder does not grow.

recall_q.en: In which process does entropy stay constant?

explain_simple.en: Entropy = messiness of energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Boyle's law: pV = constant at constant temperature. Charles's law: V/T = constant at constant pressure.

why.en: These two combine into the ideal gas law pV = mRT.

recall_q.en: Boyle's law holds at constant what?

explain_simple.en: Squeeze a gas at same temperature: pressure up, volume down.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Heat and work are path functions.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Zeroth law: if A and B are each in thermal balance with C, then A and B are in thermal balance with each other.

why.en: This is the basis of temperature measurement with a thermometer.

recall_q.en: Which law is the basis of the thermometer?

explain_simple.en: If two things match a thermometer, they match each other.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: First law: energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only changed from one form to another.

why.en: Heat from fuel becomes work plus heat lost — nothing vanishes.

recall_q.en: First law of thermodynamics is the law of?

explain_simple.en: Energy only changes form.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: First law for a closed system: Q = ΔU + W (heat supplied = rise in internal energy + work done).

why.en: Heat goes partly into warming the gas, partly into pushing the piston.

recall_q.en: Write the first law for a closed system.

explain_simple.en: Heat in = energy stored + work out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: For a cycle, net heat = net work (∮δQ = ∮δW).

why.en: After a full cycle the gas is back to its start, so ΔU = 0.

recall_q.en: In a complete cycle, net heat equals?

explain_simple.en: Over one full cycle, heat in − heat out = work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A perpetual motion machine of the first kind (PMM-1) makes work without any energy input. The first law says it is impossible.

why.en: Energy cannot come from nothing.

recall_q.en: Which law forbids PMM-1?

explain_simple.en: No machine gives free energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Second law (Kelvin–Planck): no engine working in a cycle can turn all heat into work. Some heat must go to a cold sink.

why.en: Every heat engine must throw away some heat.

example.en: A car engine loses heat through the radiator and exhaust.

recall_q.en: Which law says no engine is 100% efficient?

explain_simple.en: Some heat is always wasted.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Second law (Clausius): heat cannot flow from a cold body to a hot body by itself without outside work.

why.en: A refrigerator needs a compressor (work) to move heat out.

recall_q.en: Which statement of the second law is linked to refrigerators?

explain_simple.en: Heat flows downhill unless you pump it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: PMM-2 is an engine that turns all heat into work with one heat source. The second law says it is impossible.

why.en: It would need no cold sink.

recall_q.en: PMM-2 violates which law?

explain_simple.en: You cannot turn all heat into work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Third law: entropy of a perfect crystal at absolute zero (0 K) is zero.

why.en: At 0 K there is no molecular motion, so no disorder.

recall_q.en: At what temperature is entropy of a perfect crystal zero?

explain_simple.en: Coldest possible = no disorder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Heat engine efficiency η = Work output / Heat supplied = 1 − Q₂/Q₁.

why.en: Q₂ is the heat thrown away.

recall_q.en: Efficiency of a heat engine?

explain_simple.en: Useful work ÷ heat put in.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: COP of a refrigerator = heat removed / work input. COP of a heat pump = heat delivered / work input = COP(ref) + 1.

why.en: A heat pump delivers both the removed heat and the work.

recall_q.en: COP of heat pump in terms of COP of refrigerator?

explain_simple.en: A heat pump's COP is one more than a fridge's.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

points.en: First: energy conserved, Q = ΔU + W; no PMM-1.
Second: Kelvin–Planck (no 100% engine), Clausius (fridge needs work); no PMM-2.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Constant volume (isochoric) process: volume does not change, so no work is done (W = 0).

why.en: Work needs the boundary to move.

example.en: Heating gas in a closed rigid tank.

recall_q.en: Work done in a constant volume process?

explain_simple.en: No movement, no work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Constant pressure (isobaric) process: W = p (V₂ − V₁).

why.en: Force stays the same while the piston moves.

recall_q.en: Work in a constant pressure process?

explain_simple.en: Pressure × change in volume.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Isothermal process: temperature stays constant, pV = constant. W = p₁V₁ ln(V₂/V₁).

why.en: Heat added equals work done, so temperature does not rise.

recall_q.en: Equation of an isothermal process?

explain_simple.en: Same temperature throughout.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In an isothermal process of an ideal gas, ΔU = 0, so Q = W.

why.en: Internal energy depends only on temperature, which does not change.
