recall_q.en: In isothermal expansion, heat supplied equals?

explain_simple.en: All the heat goes into work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Adiabatic process: no heat crosses the boundary (Q = 0). Reversible adiabatic is called isentropic: pV^γ = constant.

why.en: With no heat flow, work comes from internal energy.

recall_q.en: Equation of an isentropic process?

explain_simple.en: No heat in or out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Work in an adiabatic process W = (p₁V₁ − p₂V₂)/(γ − 1). Polytropic: W = (p₁V₁ − p₂V₂)/(n − 1).

why.en: Same form, only the index changes.

recall_q.en: Work done in adiabatic expansion?

explain_simple.en: Pressure-volume difference divided by (γ − 1).

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Polytropic process: pVⁿ = constant. n = 0 constant pressure, n = 1 isothermal, n = γ adiabatic, n = ∞ constant volume.

why.en: One formula covers all the basic processes.

recall_q.en: For which value of n is pVⁿ = C an isothermal process?

explain_simple.en: Change n to get every process.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: On a PV diagram, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve.

why.en: γ (1.4) is bigger than 1, so pressure changes faster with volume.

recall_q.en: Which curve is steeper on a PV diagram: adiabatic or isothermal?

explain_simple.en: Adiabatic falls faster.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Area under a curve on a PV diagram = work done. Area enclosed by a cycle = net work of the cycle.

why.en: Work = ∫p dV, which is an area.

recall_q.en: What does the area of a closed loop on a PV diagram represent?

recall_a.en: Net work done in the cycle.

explain_simple.en: Bigger loop, more work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Throttling process: fluid passes through a narrow valve; enthalpy stays constant (h₁ = h₂) and no work is done.

why.en: Pressure drops, but no heat or work crosses.

example.en: The expansion valve in a car's AC.

recall_q.en: What stays constant in throttling?

explain_simple.en: Squeezing through a small hole drops pressure but keeps enthalpy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Free expansion: gas expands into vacuum. Work done = 0 and heat = 0.

why.en: Nothing resists the expansion, so no work.

recall_q.en: Work done in free expansion?

explain_simple.en: Expanding into nothing does no work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Isentropic: pV^γ = C, Q = 0, steeper curve.
Polytropic pVⁿ = C; throttling h = const.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air standard cycle assumptions: working fluid is air (ideal gas), constant specific heats, heat added from outside, processes reversible, no intake or exhaust losses.

why.en: These make the cycle easy to calculate.

recall_q.en: In an air standard cycle, what is the working fluid assumed to be?

explain_simple.en: Pretend the engine runs on clean air only.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carnot cycle: two isothermal and two adiabatic (isentropic) processes. It has the highest possible efficiency.

why.en: It is fully reversible, so no energy is wasted by friction.

recall_q.en: Carnot cycle consists of which processes?

explain_simple.en: The perfect, ideal engine cycle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T₂/T₁ (temperatures in kelvin).

why.en: It depends only on the hot and cold temperatures.

recall_q.en: Carnot efficiency formula?

explain_simple.en: Bigger gap between hot and cold = better efficiency.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carnot cycle is not used in real engines. Isothermal processes are too slow and adiabatic ones too fast to achieve in one engine.

why.en: The net work is also very small for the size of the engine.

recall_q.en: Is a practical engine built on the Carnot cycle?

recall_a.en: No — it is only a standard for comparison.

explain_simple.en: Perfect on paper, impossible in real life.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Otto cycle (petrol engine): 2 adiabatic + 2 constant volume processes. Heat is added at constant volume.

why.en: Spark ignition burns the mixture very quickly, while the piston is almost still.

recall_q.en: In the Otto cycle, heat is added at constant?

explain_simple.en: Petrol engine cycle: quick burn at constant volume.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Otto cycle efficiency η = 1 − 1/r^(γ−1). r = compression ratio.

why.en: Higher compression ratio squeezes more work out of the same heat.

recall_q.en: Otto efficiency depends only on what?

explain_simple.en: More squeeze, more efficiency.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel cycle: 2 adiabatic, 1 constant pressure (heat added) and 1 constant volume (heat rejected).

why.en: Fuel is injected gradually and burns while the piston moves down.

recall_q.en: In the Diesel cycle, heat is added at constant?

explain_simple.en: Diesel cycle: steady burn at constant pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cut-off ratio ρ = V₃/V₂ in a Diesel cycle: volume when fuel injection stops ÷ clearance volume. Larger cut-off ratio lowers efficiency.

why.en: Heat added late in the stroke has less chance to do work.

recall_q.en: Effect of increasing cut-off ratio on Diesel efficiency?

explain_simple.en: Burning fuel too late wastes it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: For the same compression ratio, Otto is more efficient than Diesel. For the same maximum pressure, Diesel is more efficient.

why.en: Diesel engines can use much higher compression ratios.

recall_q.en: Same compression ratio: which is more efficient, Otto or Diesel?

explain_simple.en: Same squeeze: petrol wins. Same peak pressure: diesel wins.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dual combustion (mixed or limited pressure) cycle: heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure.

why.en: Modern high-speed diesel engines burn this way.

recall_q.en: Cycle with heat added at both constant volume and constant pressure?

explain_simple.en: Half Otto, half Diesel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Joule (Brayton) cycle: 2 adiabatic and 2 constant pressure processes. Used in gas turbines and jet engines.

why.en: Gas turbines burn fuel continuously at constant pressure.

recall_q.en: Gas turbines work on which cycle?

explain_simple.en: The jet engine cycle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Joule cycle efficiency η = 1 − 1/rp^((γ−1)/γ). rp = pressure ratio.

why.en: Higher pressure ratio gives higher efficiency.

recall_q.en: Joule cycle efficiency depends on?

explain_simple.en: More pressure rise, more efficiency.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compression ratio r = total cylinder volume / clearance volume = (Vs + Vc)/Vc.

why.en: It shows how much the mixture is squeezed.

example.en: Petrol engine 8–12. Diesel engine 14–22.

recall_q.en: Compression ratio formula?

explain_simple.en: Big volume ÷ small volume.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Petrol engines use low compression ratios (about 8–12) to avoid knocking. Diesel engines need high ratios (about 14–22) to self-ignite fuel.

why.en: Diesel relies on hot compressed air to light the fuel.

recall_q.en: Typical compression ratio of a diesel engine?

explain_simple.en: Diesel squeezes much harder than petrol.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stirling cycle: 2 isothermal and 2 constant volume processes, with a regenerator. Ericsson cycle: 2 isothermal and 2 constant pressure.

why.en: With perfect regeneration both reach Carnot efficiency.

recall_q.en: Stirling cycle has which processes?

explain_simple.en: Stirling = isothermal + constant volume.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mean effective pressure (MEP) = net work of cycle / swept volume.

why.en: It is the steady pressure that would give the same work in one stroke.

recall_q.en: MEP formula?

explain_simple.en: Average push on the piston.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A petrol engine has compression ratio 8. Find air-standard efficiency (γ = 1.4).

explain.en: Use a calculator: 8 to the power 0.4.

recall_q.en: Air-standard efficiency of an Otto engine with r = 8?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A Carnot engine works between 327°C and 27°C. Find its efficiency.
Change to kelvin: T₁ = 327 + 273 = 600 K, T₂ = 27 + 273 = 300 K.

explain.en: Always use kelvin in Carnot formula.

recall_q.en: Carnot efficiency between 600 K and 300 K?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Otto: heat at constant volume, η = 1 − 1/r^(γ−1).
Diesel: heat at constant pressure; cut-off ratio.
Same r: Otto > Dual > Diesel efficiency.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An internal combustion (IC) engine burns fuel inside the cylinder. An external combustion engine burns fuel outside (e.g. steam engine).

why.en: In IC engines the hot gases push the piston directly.

recall_q.en: Is a steam engine IC or EC?

explain_simple.en: IC = fire inside. EC = fire outside.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Petrol engine = spark ignition (SI). Diesel engine = compression ignition (CI).

why.en: Petrol is lit by a spark plug; diesel lights from the heat of squeezed air.

recall_q.en: How is fuel ignited in a diesel engine?

recall_a.en: By heat of compressed air (compression ignition).

explain_simple.en: Petrol needs a spark; diesel needs squeeze.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Four-stroke engine strokes in order: suction, compression, power, exhaust.

why.en: Each stroke is half a turn, so one cycle = 2 crank turns.

recall_q.en: Order of strokes in a four-stroke engine?

explain_simple.en: Suck, squeeze, bang, blow.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A four-stroke engine gives one power stroke every 2 revolutions of the crankshaft. A two-stroke engine gives one every revolution.

why.en: Two-stroke engines merge suction and exhaust into the other strokes.

recall_q.en: Power strokes per revolution in a two-stroke engine?

explain_simple.en: Two-stroke fires every turn; four-stroke every second turn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In a four-stroke engine, the camshaft turns at half the crankshaft speed.

why.en: Each valve opens once per cycle, and one cycle is 2 crank turns.

recall_q.en: Camshaft speed compared to crankshaft in a four-stroke engine?

explain_simple.en: Crank turns twice; cam turns once.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In a petrol engine, the suction stroke draws in an air–petrol mixture. In a diesel engine, it draws in air only.

why.en: Diesel is injected later, at the end of compression.

recall_q.en: What enters a diesel engine during suction?

explain_simple.en: Petrol: mix enters. Diesel: only air enters.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two-stroke engines use ports (holes in the cylinder wall) instead of valves: inlet, transfer and exhaust ports.

why.en: The piston itself opens and closes the ports as it moves.

example.en: Old scooters and autorickshaws used two-stroke engines.

recall_q.en: What opens and closes the ports in a two-stroke engine?

explain_simple.en: The piston slides past holes to let gas in and out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In a two-stroke petrol engine, the crankcase is sealed and used to pre-compress the fresh mixture.

why.en: The pressurised mixture then rushes through the transfer port into the cylinder.

recall_q.en: In a two-stroke petrol engine, where is the mixture first compressed?

explain_simple.en: The bottom box squeezes the mix before sending it up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Scavenging is pushing out burnt gases with fresh charge in a two-stroke engine.

why.en: There is no separate exhaust stroke, so fresh charge sweeps out the old.

recall_q.en: What is scavenging?

recall_a.en: Clearing exhaust gases from the cylinder using fresh charge.

explain_simple.en: New air pushes old smoke out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A deflector-top piston directs fresh charge upward in cross-scavenged two-stroke engines.

why.en: It stops fresh mixture going straight out of the exhaust port.

recall_q.en: Why do some two-stroke pistons have a deflector on top?

recall_a.en: To guide fresh charge up and reduce loss through the exhaust port.

explain_simple.en: A bump on the piston steers the fresh mix.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two-stroke vs four-stroke: two-stroke is lighter, simpler and more powerful for its size, but uses more fuel and pollutes more.

why.en: Some fresh fuel escapes with the exhaust, and oil is burnt with fuel.

recall_q.en: Which is more fuel-efficient: two-stroke or four-stroke?

explain_simple.en: Two-stroke: light and peppy, but thirsty and smoky.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two-stroke petrol engines are lubricated by mixing oil with petrol (petroil), about 2–3%.

why.en: The crankcase holds mixture, so it cannot hold an oil sump.

recall_q.en: How is a small two-stroke petrol engine lubricated?

explain_simple.en: Oil goes in with the petrol.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel engines are heavier and costlier but more fuel-efficient and give more torque than petrol engines.

why.en: High compression ratio and lean burning give better efficiency.

recall_q.en: Which engine gives better fuel economy: petrol or diesel?

explain_simple.en: Diesel: heavy and strong, but saves fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: TDC (top dead centre) is the top-most piston position. BDC (bottom dead centre) is the bottom-most.

why.en: At these points the piston stops and reverses direction.

recall_q.en: What is TDC?

recall_a.en: Top dead centre — piston's highest position.

explain_simple.en: Top stop and bottom stop of the piston.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stroke = distance between TDC and BDC = 2 × crank radius. Bore = cylinder diameter.

why.en: The crank throw sets how far the piston travels.

recall_q.en: Stroke length in terms of crank radius?

explain_simple.en: Stroke = how far the piston travels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Swept volume Vs = (π/4) × D² × L. Engine capacity (cc) = swept volume × number of cylinders.

why.en: It is the volume the piston sweeps in one stroke.

example.en: A 150 cc motorcycle sweeps 150 cm³ per stroke.

recall_q.en: Formula for swept volume?

explain_simple.en: Cylinder area × stroke.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Square engine: bore = stroke. Over-square (short stroke): bore > stroke. Under-square (long stroke): bore < stroke.

why.en: Short stroke engines rev higher; long stroke give more low-speed torque.

recall_q.en: An engine with bore greater than stroke is called?

explain_simple.en: Wide and short = over-square.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clearance volume is the space left above the piston at TDC.

why.en: The combustion chamber is this space.

recall_q.en: Volume above the piston at TDC is called?

explain_simple.en: The small room left at the top.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve timing diagram shows, in crank degrees, when inlet and exhaust valves open and close.

why.en: Valves do not open exactly at TDC/BDC; early and late opening improves breathing.

recall_q.en: What does a valve timing diagram show?

recall_a.en: Crank angles at which valves open and close.

explain_simple.en: A clock face for the valves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Inlet valve opens about 10–20° before TDC and closes about 30–50° after BDC.

why.en: Opening early and closing late lets more charge fill the cylinder (gas inertia).

recall_q.en: Does the inlet valve close before or after BDC?

explain_simple.en: Inlet opens early and shuts late to fill more.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust valve opens about 40–50° before BDC and closes about 10–20° after TDC.

why.en: Early opening lets high-pressure gas escape; late closing clears the cylinder fully.

recall_q.en: Does the exhaust valve open before or after BDC?

explain_simple.en: Exhaust opens early to let gas out quickly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve overlap is the period when both inlet and exhaust valves are open together, near TDC.

why.en: Outgoing exhaust helps pull in fresh charge.

recall_q.en: When are both valves open together?

recall_a.en: During valve overlap, near TDC (end of exhaust, start of suction).

explain_simple.en: A short moment when both doors are open.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve lead: valve opens before the dead centre. Valve lag: valve closes after the dead centre.

why.en: Lead and lag improve breathing at high speed.

recall_q.en: Valve opening before dead centre is called?

explain_simple.en: Lead = early. Lag = late.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ignition timing: the spark occurs before TDC (spark advance). In diesel engines, injection starts before TDC.

why.en: Burning takes time, so it must start early to peak just after TDC.

recall_q.en: Does the spark occur before or after TDC?

explain_simple.en: Light the fire a little early.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Knocking in petrol engines (detonation) is sudden self-ignition of the last part of the mixture, causing a metallic noise.

why.en: Too much heat and pressure ahead of the flame.

recall_q.en: Rating of petrol against knocking?

explain_simple.en: Pinking noise = mixture exploding on its own.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Octane number rates petrol's anti-knock quality (iso-octane = 100, n-heptane = 0). Cetane number rates diesel's ignition quality (cetane = 100).

why.en: Petrol should resist self-ignition; diesel should self-ignite easily.

recall_q.en: Ignition quality of diesel is rated by?

explain_simple.en: Octane for petrol, cetane for diesel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel knock is caused by a long ignition delay: too much fuel collects before burning, then explodes.

why.en: Petrol knock happens late in combustion; diesel knock happens at the start.

recall_q.en: Main cause of diesel knock?

explain_simple.en: Fuel waits too long, then bangs.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Things that reduce petrol knock lead to more diesel knock, and vice versa. For example, high compression ratio reduces diesel knock but increases petrol knock.

why.en: Diesel needs easy self-ignition; petrol must avoid it.

recall_q.en: Does high compression ratio increase or reduce diesel knock?

explain_simple.en: Petrol and diesel need opposite things.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: On the PV diagram of an actual four-stroke engine, the small negative loop at the bottom is the pumping loss loop (suction and exhaust).

why.en: Work is spent pulling in charge and pushing out gases.

recall_q.en: What does the small lower loop on a four-stroke PV diagram show?

explain_simple.en: Breathing costs some work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Firing order of a common 4-cylinder in-line engine: 1-3-4-2 (or 1-2-4-3).

why.en: Spreads power strokes evenly and balances the crankshaft.

recall_q.en: Common firing order of a four-cylinder engine?

explain_simple.en: Fire cylinders in a balanced order, not 1-2-3-4.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wankel (rotary) engine uses a triangular rotor instead of a piston.

why.en: The rotor turns in an oval housing to make the four strokes.

recall_q.en: What replaces the piston in a Wankel engine?

explain_simple.en: A spinning triangle instead of an up-down piston.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing

points.en: Four-stroke: suck, squeeze, power, exhaust; 1 power stroke per 2 turns.
Two-stroke: ports, crankcase compression, scavenging, petroil.
IVO before TDC, IVC after BDC; EVO before BDC, EVC after TDC.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Indicated power (IP) is power developed by the gas inside the cylinder. IP = p_m L A n k / 60 (n = power strokes per minute).

why.en: It is measured from the indicator diagram.

recall_q.en: Power developed inside the engine cylinder is called?

explain_simple.en: Power made by burning gas.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake power (BP) is the useful power at the crankshaft. BP = 2πNT / 60.

why.en: It is measured with a brake (dynamometer).

recall_q.en: Formula of brake power?

explain_simple.en: Power you actually get at the shaft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Frictional power FP = IP − BP.

why.en: Some of the gas power is lost in rubbing parts and driving pumps.

recall_q.en: Frictional power = ?

explain_simple.en: What friction eats.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mechanical efficiency ηm = BP / IP.

why.en: It shows how much gas power reaches the shaft.

example.en: IP 50 kW, BP 40 kW → ηm = 80%.

recall_q.en: Mechanical efficiency formula?

explain_simple.en: Shaft power ÷ cylinder power.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Indicated thermal efficiency = IP / (fuel mass per second × calorific value).

why.en: Compares gas power with energy in fuel.

recall_q.en: Indicated thermal efficiency = ?

explain_simple.en: Cylinder power ÷ fuel energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake thermal efficiency = BP / (mf × CV). Brake thermal efficiency = mechanical efficiency × indicated thermal efficiency.

why.en: Fuel energy → gas power → shaft power.

recall_q.en: Brake thermal efficiency = ?

explain_simple.en: Shaft power ÷ fuel energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Relative efficiency (efficiency ratio) = actual thermal efficiency / air standard efficiency.

why.en: It shows how close a real engine comes to its ideal cycle.

recall_q.en: Relative efficiency = ?

recall_a.en: Actual thermal efficiency ÷ air standard efficiency.

explain_simple.en: How near the real engine is to the ideal.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific fuel consumption (SFC) = fuel used per hour / brake power. Unit: kg/kWh. Lower SFC = better engine.

why.en: It shows fuel needed for each unit of power.

recall_q.en: Is a lower or higher SFC better?

explain_simple.en: Less fuel for the same work is better.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Volumetric efficiency = actual volume of air drawn in / swept volume (at intake conditions).

why.en: Shows how well the engine breathes.

example.en: Naturally aspirated engines get 70–90%; turbocharged can exceed 100%.

recall_q.en: Volumetric efficiency compares what?

recall_a.en: Actual air drawn in with swept volume.

explain_simple.en: How full the cylinder really gets.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A dynamometer measures brake power. Types: rope brake, Prony brake (absorption), hydraulic, eddy current, and transmission dynamometers.

why.en: It applies a measured load to the shaft.

recall_q.en: Instrument used to measure brake power?

explain_simple.en: A machine that loads the engine to measure its power.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Engine indicator draws the actual PV (indicator) diagram of a running engine. Its area gives indicated work.

why.en: IP is found from the indicator diagram.

recall_q.en: Which instrument draws the PV diagram of a running engine?

explain_simple.en: It traces pressure against volume while the engine runs.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Morse test finds IP of a multi-cylinder engine. Each cylinder is cut off in turn, and the fall in BP gives that cylinder's IP.

why.en: Cutting one cylinder at constant speed leaves friction the same.

recall_q.en: Morse test is used for what kind of engine?

explain_simple.en: Switch off one cylinder at a time and see how much power drops.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In the Morse test, IP of one cylinder = total BP − BP with that cylinder cut off. Sum for all cylinders gives engine IP.

why.en: The missing power is what that cylinder gave.

recall_q.en: IP of cylinder 1 in Morse test?

explain_simple.en: Power lost = power that cylinder was making.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Willan's line method (fuel rate extrapolation) finds frictional power of a diesel engine by plotting fuel consumption against BP and extending the line to zero fuel.

why.en: The negative BP where fuel is zero equals the friction power.

recall_q.en: Willan's line method finds what?

explain_simple.en: Draw the fuel line back to zero to find friction.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Motoring test: the engine is driven by an electric motor without firing; motor power needed = frictional power.

why.en: With no combustion, the motor only overcomes friction and pumping.

recall_q.en: Which test drives an engine with a motor to find friction power?

explain_simple.en: Spin the engine with a motor; the motor's effort is friction.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Heat balance sheet shows where fuel heat goes: brake power, cooling water, exhaust gases and unaccounted losses.

why.en: It helps find and reduce waste.

recall_q.en: Name the heads in a heat balance sheet.

recall_a.en: BP, cooling water, exhaust, unaccounted losses.

explain_simple.en: A bill showing where every unit of fuel heat went.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A typical petrol engine turns only about 25–30% of fuel heat into brake power. About 30% goes to cooling and about 35% to exhaust.

why.en: Most heat is lost, as the second law says.

recall_q.en: Roughly what share of fuel heat becomes useful power in a petrol engine?

explain_simple.en: Only about a quarter becomes motion.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Calorific value is the heat released by burning 1 kg of fuel. Petrol and diesel are about 42–44 MJ/kg.

why.en: It is used to find fuel energy in efficiency calculations.

recall_q.en: Approximate calorific value of petrol?

explain_simple.en: Energy packed in 1 kg of fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stoichiometric (chemically correct) air–fuel ratio for petrol is about 14.7 : 1 by mass.

why.en: That much air exactly burns all the fuel.

recall_q.en: Chemically correct air-fuel ratio for petrol?

explain_simple.en: About 15 kg of air for 1 kg of petrol.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Torque is turning force at the crankshaft (N·m). Power = torque × speed.

why.en: Same torque at higher rpm gives more power.

recall_q.en: Relation between power and torque?

explain_simple.en: Torque = twist; power = twist × speed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: 1 metric horsepower = 735.5 W. 1 kW ≈ 1.36 metric hp.

why.en: Vehicle brochures give power in hp, PS or kW.

recall_q.en: 1 metric hp is how many watts?

explain_simple.en: One horse ≈ three-quarters of a kilowatt.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: An engine has IP = 50 kW and FP = 10 kW. Find BP and mechanical efficiency.

recall_q.en: IP 50 kW, BP 40 kW: mechanical efficiency?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: Engine torque is 100 N·m at 3000 rpm. Find brake power.

explain.en: Divide watts by 1000 for kW.

recall_q.en: Formula used to find BP from torque and rpm?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

points.en: IP inside, BP at shaft, FP = IP − BP.
Morse test (multi-cylinder IP), Willan's line, heat balance sheet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An air compressor takes in air at low pressure and delivers it at high pressure.

why.en: Work is done on the air to squeeze it.

recall_q.en: What does a compressor do?

recall_a.en: Raises the pressure of air (or gas).

explain_simple.en: It squeezes air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Uses of compressed air in vehicles: air brakes, air suspension, tyre inflation, door opening in buses, horns, paint spraying in workshops.

why.en: Compressed air stores energy and is safe and clean.

example.en: KSRTC buses use air brakes and air-operated doors.

recall_q.en: Give one automobile use of compressed air.

recall_a.en: Air brakes (also tyre inflation, air suspension, doors).

explain_simple.en: Air brakes in buses run on compressed air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Types of compressors: reciprocating (piston), rotary (vane, screw, lobe/roots), centrifugal and axial.

why.en: Reciprocating gives high pressure; rotary gives large steady flow.

recall_q.en: Which compressor type uses a piston?

explain_simple.en: Piston type for high pressure, rotary type for lots of air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Single acting compressor: air is compressed on one side of the piston. Double acting: on both sides.

why.en: Double acting delivers twice the air per revolution.

recall_q.en: In a double-acting compressor, air is compressed on how many sides of the piston?

explain_simple.en: Double acting works both ways.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Single stage compressor: air compressed to final pressure in one cylinder. Multi-stage: in two or more cylinders with intercooling.

why.en: High pressure in one stage makes air too hot and wastes work.

recall_q.en: Why use multi-stage compression for high pressure?

recall_a.en: Saves work and keeps temperature low (with intercooling).

explain_simple.en: Squeeze in steps and cool in between.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An intercooler cools air between stages of a multi-stage compressor.

why.en: Cooler air is easier to compress, so work is saved.

recall_q.en: What is the job of an intercooler?

recall_a.en: To cool air between compression stages.

explain_simple.en: Cool the air before squeezing again.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Perfect intercooling: air is cooled back to its starting temperature after each stage.

why.en: This gives the least total work.

recall_q.en: What is perfect intercooling?

recall_a.en: Cooling air to initial (suction) temperature after each stage.

explain_simple.en: Bring air back to start temperature each time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: For least work in a two-stage compressor, intermediate pressure p₂ = √(p₁ × p₃).

why.en: This divides the work equally between the two stages.

recall_q.en: Ideal intermediate pressure in a two-stage compressor?

explain_simple.en: Middle pressure = square root of first × last.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compression work is least for isothermal compression and most for adiabatic compression.

why.en: Hot air resists squeezing; keeping it cool lowers work.

recall_q.en: Which compression needs the least work?

explain_simple.en: Cool squeezing is easiest.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Isothermal efficiency of a compressor = isothermal work / actual work.

why.en: It compares the real compressor with the ideal minimum work.

recall_q.en: Isothermal efficiency = ?

explain_simple.en: Ideal work ÷ real work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Volumetric efficiency of a reciprocating compressor falls as clearance volume and pressure ratio rise.

why.en: Compressed air left in the clearance re-expands and blocks fresh air.

recall_q.en: Effect of more clearance on compressor volumetric efficiency?

explain_simple.en: Leftover air takes the place of new air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Free air delivered (FAD) is the compressed air output, expressed as volume at atmospheric conditions.

why.en: This makes compressors of different makes comparable.

recall_q.en: What is FAD?

recall_a.en: Free air delivered — output volume at atmospheric conditions.

explain_simple.en: How much normal air the compressor takes in and delivers.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Roots blower (lobe compressor) has no internal compression; it moves air and pressure rises at delivery. Used as superchargers.

why.en: Two lobes trap air and carry it round.

recall_q.en: Which rotary compressor is used as a supercharger with two lobes?

explain_simple.en: Two spinning lobes push air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Centrifugal compressors (turbochargers) use a fast-spinning impeller to throw air outward and raise its pressure.

why.en: Air speed is turned into pressure in the diffuser.

recall_q.en: Turbochargers use which type of compressor?

explain_simple.en: A spinning wheel flings air to squeeze it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Compressor raises air pressure; uses: air brakes, tyres, doors.
Reciprocating, rotary (vane, screw, roots), centrifugal, axial.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Heat moves in three ways: conduction, convection and radiation.

why.en: Heat always flows from hot to cold.

recall_q.en: Three modes of heat transfer?

explain_simple.en: Touch, flow, rays.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Conduction is heat passing through a solid from particle to particle, with no movement of the material.

why.en: Hot particles vibrate and pass energy to their neighbours.

example.en: A steel spoon in hot tea gets hot at the handle.

recall_q.en: Heat through a solid by contact is called?

explain_simple.en: Heat passes hand to hand.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Convection is heat carried by moving fluid (liquid or gas).

why.en: Hot fluid becomes lighter and rises; cold fluid sinks.

example.en: Coolant carries heat from the engine to the radiator. Sea breeze.

recall_q.en: Heat carried by a moving fluid is called?

explain_simple.en: The fluid itself carries the heat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Natural (free) convection: fluid moves due to density difference. Forced convection: a fan or pump moves the fluid.

why.en: A radiator fan forces air through the core.

recall_q.en: A radiator with a fan uses which convection?

explain_simple.en: Natural = by itself. Forced = by a fan or pump.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Radiation is heat travelling as electromagnetic waves. It needs no medium and can cross vacuum.

why.en: This is how the Sun's heat reaches Earth.

recall_q.en: Which mode of heat transfer works in vacuum?

explain_simple.en: Heat rays travel even through empty space.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fourier's law of conduction: Q = −k A (dT/dx). Heat flow is proportional to area and temperature gradient.

why.en: Steeper temperature drop pushes more heat through.

recall_q.en: Which law governs heat conduction?

explain_simple.en: More area and bigger temperature drop = more heat flow.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermal conductivity (k) is a material's ability to conduct heat. Unit: W/m·K.

why.en: It appears in Fourier's law.

recall_q.en: SI unit of thermal conductivity?

explain_simple.en: How easily heat passes through a material.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Silver and copper have very high thermal conductivity. Air, wood and glass wool have low k (insulators).

why.en: Free electrons in metals carry heat quickly.

example.en: Radiators use copper or aluminium. Silencer heat shields use insulation.

recall_q.en: Which metal has the highest thermal conductivity?

explain_simple.en: Metals pass heat fast; air and wool slow it down.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Newton's law of cooling: convection heat Q = h A (Ts − T∞). h = heat transfer coefficient (W/m²K).

why.en: Heat loss depends on surface area and temperature difference.

recall_q.en: Law used for convection heat transfer?

recall_a.en: Newton's law of cooling, Q = hAΔT.

explain_simple.en: Bigger surface and bigger temperature gap = faster cooling.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stefan–Boltzmann law: radiation energy E = σ T⁴. σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/m²K⁴.

why.en: Double the absolute temperature → 16 times the radiation.

recall_q.en: Radiation emitted is proportional to temperature to which power?

explain_simple.en: A bit hotter gives off much more radiation.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A black body absorbs all radiation falling on it and is the best emitter. Emissivity of a black body = 1.

why.en: Dark, rough surfaces absorb and emit well; shiny ones do not.

example.en: Radiators are painted black to give off heat better.

recall_q.en: Emissivity of a perfect black body?

explain_simple.en: Black absorbs and gives off heat best.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Kirchhoff's law: at thermal equilibrium, emissivity of a body equals its absorptivity.

why.en: Good absorbers are good emitters.

recall_q.en: Which law says emissivity = absorptivity?

explain_simple.en: A good absorber is a good emitter.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermal resistance of a plane wall R = L/(kA). Walls in series: resistances add.

why.en: Like electric resistance, it opposes heat flow.

recall_q.en: Thermal resistance of a plane wall?

explain_simple.en: Thicker wall or poorer conductor = more resistance.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Heat exchanger types: parallel flow (both fluids same direction) and counter flow (opposite directions). Counter flow is more effective.

why.en: In counter flow the temperature difference stays more even along the length.

example.en: A car radiator is a cross-flow heat exchanger.

recall_q.en: Which heat exchanger is more effective: parallel or counter flow?

explain_simple.en: Fluids moving opposite ways swap heat better.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fins are extended surfaces that increase heat transfer area.

why.en: More area lets more heat escape by convection.

example.en: Fins on motorcycle engine cylinders.

recall_q.en: Why do air-cooled engines have fins?

recall_a.en: To increase surface area for heat loss.

explain_simple.en: Fins give heat more room to leave.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Fourier: Q = −kA dT/dx; k in W/m·K.
Newton cooling Q = hAΔT; Stefan–Boltzmann E = σT⁴.
Black body emissivity = 1; Kirchhoff: ε = α.
Fins add area; counter flow best.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Engines are classified by fuel (petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG), ignition (SI, CI), strokes (2, 4), cooling (air, water), cylinder layout (inline, V, flat/opposed, radial) and valve position.

why.en: PSC often asks one of these classification bases.

recall_q.en: Name two bases for classifying IC engines.

recall_a.en: Fuel, ignition, strokes, cooling, cylinder arrangement, valve position.

explain_simple.en: Engines are grouped by fuel, firing, strokes, cooling and layout.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: V-engine: two rows of cylinders in a V shape on one crankshaft. Flat (boxer): two rows lying opposite each other.

why.en: These layouts make long engines shorter and smoother.

recall_q.en: Engine with cylinders horizontally opposed is called?

explain_simple.en: V = two rows at an angle. Boxer = two rows flat, facing out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Petrol engine has a spark plug and carburettor or petrol injector. Diesel engine has a fuel injection pump and injector, and no spark plug.

why.en: The ignition method decides the parts.

recall_q.en: Which part is not found in a diesel engine: spark plug or injector?

explain_simple.en: Spark plug = petrol. Injector pump = diesel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Petrol engine power is controlled by a throttle valve (quantity governing). Diesel engine power is controlled by the amount of fuel injected (quality governing).

why.en: Diesel always takes full air; only fuel quantity changes.

recall_q.en: How is a diesel engine's power controlled?

recall_a.en: By changing the quantity of fuel injected (quality governing).

explain_simple.en: Petrol: control air-fuel mix amount. Diesel: control fuel only.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel engines run at lower speeds than petrol engines and have heavier parts.

why.en: High compression pressure needs strong, heavy parts.

recall_q.en: Which engine is heavier for the same power: petrol or diesel?

explain_simple.en: Diesel squeezes harder, so it is built heavier.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ignition delay in a diesel engine is the time between start of injection and start of combustion.

why.en: Fuel must mix with air and heat up before it lights.

recall_q.en: Time between fuel injection and start of burning is called?

explain_simple.en: The short wait before diesel catches fire.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stages of combustion in a CI engine: ignition delay, rapid (uncontrolled) combustion, controlled combustion, after-burning.

why.en: Fuel first waits, then burns all at once, then burns as it is injected.

recall_q.en: First stage of combustion in a diesel engine?

explain_simple.en: Wait, bang, steady burn, after-burn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stages of combustion in an SI engine: ignition lag (preparation), flame propagation, after-burning.

why.en: The spark starts a small flame that spreads across the chamber.

recall_q.en: Main stage of combustion in a petrol engine after ignition lag?

explain_simple.en: Spark, spread, finish.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pre-ignition is ignition of the mixture before the spark, by a hot spot such as a glowing carbon deposit or overheated plug.

why.en: Hot spots light the charge too early.

recall_q.en: Ignition caused by a hot spot before the spark is called?

explain_simple.en: Fire starts before the spark — too early.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Running-on (dieseling) is when a petrol engine keeps running after the ignition is switched off.

why.en: Hot spots keep lighting the mixture.

recall_q.en: A petrol engine running after switch-off is called?

explain_simple.en: The engine refuses to stop because it is too hot inside.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tetra-ethyl lead (TEL) was once added to petrol to stop knocking. It is now banned because lead is poisonous and damages catalytic converters.

why.en: India moved to unleaded petrol by 2000.

recall_q.en: Why was tetra-ethyl lead added to petrol?

explain_simple.en: Lead stopped knocking but poisoned the air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Supercharging is forcing more air into the cylinder than it would draw by itself. Turbocharger uses exhaust gas; supercharger is driven by the engine.

why.en: More air allows more fuel to burn, giving more power.

recall_q.en: A turbocharger is driven by what?

explain_simple.en: Pack in more air to get more power.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel combustion chambers: direct injection (open chamber) and indirect injection (pre-combustion chamber, swirl chamber).

why.en: Indirect chambers mix air and fuel better but lose more heat.

recall_q.en: Name two types of diesel combustion chamber.

recall_a.en: Direct injection (open) and indirect (pre-chamber, swirl chamber).

explain_simple.en: Fuel sprayed straight in, or into a small side room first.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Glow plugs heat the combustion chamber of indirect injection diesel engines for easy cold starting.

why.en: Cold walls take away heat needed for self-ignition.

recall_q.en: Purpose of a glow plug?

recall_a.en: To help cold starting of diesel engines.

explain_simple.en: A small heater to start a cold diesel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Squish is the squeezing of mixture out from between piston crown and head near TDC. Swirl is the rotating motion of air in the cylinder.

why.en: Both mix air and fuel better for clean, fast burning.

recall_q.en: Rotating motion of air in a cylinder is called?

explain_simple.en: Squish squeezes; swirl spins.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mean piston speed = 2 L N / 60 (m/s).

why.en: The piston covers two strokes per revolution.

recall_q.en: Mean piston speed formula?

explain_simple.en: Two strokes each turn × turns per second.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Power strokes per minute: four-stroke n = N/2; two-stroke n = N (N = rpm).

why.en: Used in the indicated power formula.

recall_q.en: Power strokes per minute in a four-stroke engine at N rpm?

explain_simple.en: Four-stroke fires at half the rpm.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fuel for SI engines must be volatile (evaporate easily). Fuel for CI engines must have good ignition quality and suitable viscosity.

why.en: Petrol must mix as vapour; diesel must self-ignite and spray well.

recall_q.en: Which property is most important for petrol: volatility or cetane?

explain_simple.en: Petrol must evaporate easily.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CNG has high octane (about 120) and suits SI engines. LPG is mainly propane and butane.

why.en: Gas fuels burn clean and resist knock.

example.en: Autorickshaws and city buses in Kochi run on CNG.

recall_q.en: Main gases in LPG?

explain_simple.en: CNG = methane; LPG = propane + butane.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CNG is mostly methane, stored at about 200 bar in cylinders.

why.en: Methane must be compressed to store enough in a small tank.

recall_q.en: Main component of CNG?

explain_simple.en: CNG is squeezed methane gas.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake mean effective pressure (bmep) = BP related to swept volume. imep relates to IP. bmep = ηm × imep.

why.en: Mean effective pressure lets engines of different sizes be compared.

recall_q.en: bmep in terms of imep?

explain_simple.en: Shaft pressure = efficiency × cylinder pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Engine performance curves plot BP, torque and SFC against speed.

why.en: Torque peaks at medium speed; BP keeps rising to a higher speed; SFC is lowest at medium load.

recall_q.en: At which speed is torque usually highest: low, medium or top?

explain_simple.en: Torque peaks in the middle, power peaks near the top.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air consumption is measured with an air box and orifice, which steadies the pulsing intake flow.

why.en: Engine intake is in pulses; the box smooths them for accurate reading.

recall_q.en: How is air flow into an engine measured on a test bed?

recall_a.en: Air box with an orifice and manometer.

explain_simple.en: A big box calms the air so it can be measured.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fuel consumption is measured with a burette: time taken to use a known volume (e.g. 50 cc) of fuel.

why.en: Volume × density ÷ time gives kg per second.

recall_q.en: Simple instrument to measure fuel consumption on a test bed?

explain_simple.en: Time how fast 50 cc of fuel is used.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Indicated thermal efficiency is always higher than brake thermal efficiency.

why.en: BP is less than IP because of friction.

recall_q.en: Which is higher: indicated or brake thermal efficiency?

explain_simple.en: Friction makes brake efficiency lower.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust gas analysers measure CO, HC, CO₂ and O₂ in petrol exhaust. Smoke meters measure diesel smoke opacity.

why.en: Used for pollution under control (PUC) testing.

recall_q.en: Diesel smoke is measured by?

explain_simple.en: Gas analyser for petrol, smoke meter for diesel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Good insulators: asbestos (now avoided), glass wool, mineral wool, cork, thermocol.

why.en: They trap air, which conducts heat poorly.

recall_q.en: Why is glass wool a good insulator?

recall_a.en: It traps still air, which conducts heat poorly.

explain_simple.en: Trapped air blocks heat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Heat transfer in an engine: gas to cylinder wall by convection and radiation, through wall by conduction, wall to coolant by convection.

why.en: All three modes work together.

recall_q.en: How does heat pass through the cylinder wall?

explain_simple.en: Gas → wall (convection/radiation), through wall (conduction), to coolant (convection).

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermos flask: double glass walls with vacuum between (stops conduction and convection) and silvered surfaces (stop radiation).

why.en: It blocks all three modes.

recall_q.en: Why are thermos flask walls silvered?

recall_a.en: To reduce heat transfer by radiation.

explain_simple.en: Shiny walls bounce heat rays back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Otto cycle efficiency rises with compression ratio, but petrol engines cannot go very high because of knocking.

why.en: High pressure and heat cause the mixture to self-ignite.

recall_q.en: What limits compression ratio in petrol engines?

explain_simple.en: Squeeze petrol too much and it knocks.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel cycle efficiency η = 1 − (1/r^(γ−1)) × [(ρ^γ − 1)/(γ(ρ − 1))].

why.en: The bracket term (always >1) makes Diesel lower than Otto for the same r.

recall_q.en: Is the Diesel efficiency term in brackets greater or less than 1?

explain_simple.en: Diesel formula = Otto formula with an extra penalty.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gas turbines can use regeneration, reheating and intercooling to raise efficiency and work output.

why.en: Regeneration reuses exhaust heat to warm air before combustion.

recall_q.en: Using exhaust heat to warm compressed air in a gas turbine is called?

explain_simple.en: Reuse waste heat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A heat engine needs: a hot source, a working fluid, and a cold sink.

why.en: Work is done only when heat flows from hot to cold.

recall_q.en: What three things does a heat engine need?

recall_a.en: Hot source, working substance, cold sink.

explain_simple.en: Hot side, cold side, and something to carry heat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Reversible process: can be reversed with no change left in system or surroundings. All real processes are irreversible.

why.en: Friction, heat transfer across a temperature gap and mixing make processes irreversible.

recall_q.en: Name one cause of irreversibility.

recall_a.en: Friction (or heat flow across finite temperature difference, mixing).

explain_simple.en: Real life always loses a little energy you cannot get back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compressor parts: cylinder, piston, inlet and delivery valves (reed or plate type), unloader, air receiver tank, safety valve.

why.en: The receiver stores air and steadies pressure.

recall_q.en: Tank that stores compressed air is called?

explain_simple.en: The storage tank for squeezed air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A governor (unloader) in a vehicle air compressor stops compression when tank pressure reaches its limit (about 7–8 bar).

why.en: It prevents over-pressure and saves engine power.

recall_q.en: What stops a vehicle air compressor at full pressure?

explain_simple.en: It tells the compressor to rest when the tank is full.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Load is the outside force acting on a body. Stress is the inside resisting force per unit area. Stress = Load / Area.

why.en: The body resists the load from inside; spreading it over the area gives stress.

example.en: A bus's weight on its axle sets up stress inside the axle.

recall_q.en: Formula for stress?

explain_simple.en: Stress = how hard each square mm is being pulled or pushed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Unit of stress: N/m² (pascal). In engineering we often use N/mm² = MPa.

why.en: Metal parts have small areas, so N/mm² is handy.

recall_q.en: 1 N/mm² equals how many MPa?

explain_simple.en: N/mm² and MPa are the same.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Strain is change in length divided by original length. Strain = δL / L. It has no unit.

why.en: Length divided by length cancels units.

recall_q.en: Unit of strain?

explain_simple.en: How much it stretches compared with its size.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tensile stress: forces pull the body and it gets longer. Compressive stress: forces push and it gets shorter.

why.en: The direction of load decides the type.

example.en: Tension: a towing rope. Compression: a car jack's column.

recall_q.en: A towing rope is under which stress?

explain_simple.en: Pull = tension. Push = compression.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Shear stress: two equal, opposite forces act along (parallel to) a surface and try to slide one part over the other. τ = P / A.

why.en: The cut tends to happen across the section.

example.en: Scissors cutting paper; a rivet in a joint; a shear pin.

recall_q.en: A rivet in a lap joint is mainly under which stress?

explain_simple.en: Shear = sliding cut, like scissors.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Shear strain is the angle change (in radians) produced by shear stress. Symbol φ.

why.en: Shear twists the shape rather than stretching it.

recall_q.en: Shear strain is measured as?

explain_simple.en: How much a square becomes a slanted box.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Longitudinal strain is strain along the load. Lateral strain is strain at right angles to the load.

why.en: When a bar stretches, it also gets thinner.

example.en: Pull a rubber band: it gets longer and thinner.

recall_q.en: Strain at right angles to load is called?

explain_simple.en: Longer one way, thinner the other.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Poisson's ratio (μ or 1/m) = lateral strain / longitudinal strain. For steel about 0.25–0.3.

why.en: It links how much a bar thins when it stretches.

recall_q.en: Poisson's ratio = ?

explain_simple.en: Thinning ÷ stretching.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Poisson's ratio lies between 0 and 0.5 for usual materials. Cork ≈ 0, rubber ≈ 0.5.

why.en: At 0.5 the volume does not change at all.

recall_q.en: Maximum value of Poisson's ratio?

explain_simple.en: Between zero and half.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Volumetric strain = change in volume / original volume. For a bar in tension: εv = ε (1 − 2μ).

why.en: It grows in length but shrinks in the other two directions.

recall_q.en: Volumetric strain of a bar under axial load?

explain_simple.en: Change in volume compared with original.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Direct (normal) stress acts at right angles to the surface. Shear stress acts along the surface.

why.en: Tension and compression are normal stresses.

recall_q.en: Is tensile stress normal or tangential?

explain_simple.en: Normal = straight in or out. Shear = sideways.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Complementary shear stress: shear stress on one plane always comes with an equal shear stress on the plane at right angles.

why.en: Otherwise the small element would spin.

recall_q.en: Shear stress on a plane is accompanied by what?

recall_a.en: Equal shear stress on the perpendicular plane.

explain_simple.en: Shear always comes in pairs.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bearing (crushing) stress is compressive stress where two parts press on each other. In a rivet: σc = P / (d × t).

why.en: The plate presses on the side of the rivet.

recall_q.en: Crushing area of a rivet?

explain_simple.en: Pressing stress at the contact face.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Strain energy is energy stored in a body when it is strained. Resilience is strain energy stored per unit volume up to the elastic limit.

why.en: A stretched spring stores energy that it gives back.

example.en: Leaf springs absorb road shocks as strain energy.

recall_q.en: Energy stored in a body due to strain is called?

explain_simple.en: Stretch something and it stores energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Strain energy U = σ² V / (2E). Proof resilience is maximum strain energy stored up to the elastic limit.

why.en: Energy rises with the square of stress.

recall_q.en: Formula for strain energy under gradual load?

explain_simple.en: Twice the stress, four times the stored energy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A suddenly applied load causes twice the stress of the same load applied gradually.

why.en: The load drops with full force before the body resists it.

recall_q.en: Stress due to a suddenly applied load compared to gradual load?

explain_simple.en: Drop a load and it hits twice as hard.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Stress = P/A (N/mm² = MPa); strain = δL/L, no unit.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A stress–strain diagram is drawn from a tensile test on a universal testing machine (UTM).

why.en: The specimen is pulled slowly until it breaks and its stretch is recorded.

recall_q.en: Machine used for a tensile test?

explain_simple.en: Pull a bar until it snaps and draw the graph.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Points on the mild steel diagram in order: limit of proportionality, elastic limit, upper yield point, lower yield point, ultimate stress, breaking point.

why.en: PSC often asks the correct order.

recall_q.en: Order of points on a mild steel stress–strain curve?

recall_a.en: Proportional limit, elastic limit, upper yield, lower yield, ultimate, breaking.

explain_simple.en: Straight, springy, yield, peak, snap.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Limit of proportionality: up to this point stress is directly proportional to strain (straight line).

why.en: Hooke's law is valid only up to here.

recall_q.en: Up to which point is Hooke's law valid?

explain_simple.en: The end of the straight part of the graph.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Elastic limit: the highest stress after which the material still returns to its original shape when the load is removed.

why.en: Beyond it, some stretch stays permanently.

recall_q.en: Beyond which point does permanent set occur?

explain_simple.en: The last point where it springs fully back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Yield point: the material stretches a lot with almost no increase in load. Mild steel has a clear upper and lower yield point.

why.en: The crystals inside start slipping.

recall_q.en: Point where strain increases with no rise in stress?

explain_simple.en: It suddenly gives way and stretches.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ultimate stress is the maximum stress a material can take. It is the highest point on the curve.

why.en: After this, necking starts and the load falls.

recall_q.en: Highest point on a stress–strain curve?

explain_simple.en: The peak strength.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Necking: after ultimate stress, a ductile bar gets thinner at one spot and breaks there.

why.en: The weakest section thins faster than the rest.

recall_q.en: Local reduction of area before breaking is called?

explain_simple.en: The bar gets a thin waist and snaps there.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Breaking stress (nominal) is lower than ultimate stress on the engineering curve, because the original area is used.

why.en: The load falls after necking, though actual stress at the neck is high.

recall_q.en: On the engineering curve, is breaking stress higher or lower than ultimate stress?

explain_simple.en: The graph drops a little before the snap.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ductile material stretches a lot before breaking (mild steel, copper, aluminium). Brittle material breaks with very little stretch (cast iron, glass, concrete).

why.en: Ductile metals have a yield point and necking; brittle ones do not.

recall_q.en: Is cast iron ductile or brittle?

explain_simple.en: Ductile bends; brittle snaps.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brittle materials have no clear yield point. Their curve is nearly straight to fracture.

why.en: They fail without plastic flow.

recall_q.en: Does cast iron show a yield point in tension?

explain_simple.en: Brittle material just breaks, no warning.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Proof stress (0.2% offset) is used as yield strength for materials without a clear yield point, like aluminium and high-tensile steel.

why.en: A line parallel to the elastic part, drawn at 0.2% strain, marks it.

recall_q.en: How is yield strength found for metals with no clear yield point?

explain_simple.en: Draw a parallel line at 0.2% to find yield.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Percentage elongation and percentage reduction in area measure ductility.

why.en: More stretch and more thinning mean more ductile.

recall_q.en: Name a measure of ductility.

explain_simple.en: How much it stretched before breaking.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Working stress (allowable stress) is the safe stress used in design. It is kept well below the failure stress.

why.en: Real loads, materials and workmanship are never perfect.

recall_q.en: Safe stress used for design is called?

explain_simple.en: The stress we plan to use, with a safety margin.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Factor of safety = ultimate stress / working stress (or yield stress / working stress for ductile metals).

why.en: It shows how much margin is kept.

example.en: Ultimate 400 MPa, working 100 MPa → FOS = 4.

recall_q.en: Factor of safety formula?

explain_simple.en: How many times stronger than needed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Factor of safety is always more than 1. It is higher for brittle materials and shock loads.

why.en: Brittle parts fail suddenly without warning.

recall_q.en: Is FOS more or less than 1?

explain_simple.en: Always build stronger than the load.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Elasticity: returns to shape after load. Plasticity: keeps the new shape. Malleability: can be hammered into sheets. Toughness: absorbs energy before breaking.

why.en: PSC asks these mechanical properties often.

recall_q.en: Property that lets a metal be beaten into thin sheets?

explain_simple.en: Ductile = drawn into wire. Malleable = beaten into sheet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hardness is resistance to scratching, wear and indentation. Tests: Brinell, Rockwell, Vickers.

why.en: A hard surface lasts longer in bearings and gears.

recall_q.en: Name a hardness test.

explain_simple.en: How hard it is to dent or scratch.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Impact tests (Izod, Charpy) measure toughness — energy absorbed when a notched specimen is broken by a swinging hammer.

why.en: Vehicle parts face sudden shocks.

recall_q.en: Izod and Charpy tests measure what?

explain_simple.en: Hit it with a hammer and see how much energy it takes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fatigue: failure under repeated (cyclic) loading at stress below the ultimate strength. Endurance limit is the stress below which it never fails.

why.en: Tiny cracks grow with each cycle.

example.en: Axles and crankshafts can fail by fatigue.

recall_q.en: Failure under repeated loads below ultimate stress is called?

explain_simple.en: Bend a wire again and again and it breaks.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Creep: slow permanent stretching under a constant load over a long time, especially at high temperature.

why.en: Hot metal slowly flows.

example.en: Turbine blades and exhaust valves can creep.

recall_q.en: Slow deformation under steady load at high temperature?

explain_simple.en: Hot metal slowly sags under load.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Worked example: stress and factor of safety

text.en: Question: A steel rod of area 100 mm² carries 20 kN. Ultimate stress is 400 N/mm². Find stress and FOS.
