summary.en: σ = P/A — keep units N and mm².

recall_q.en: Ultimate 400 N/mm², working 200 N/mm²: FOS?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety

points.en: Proportional limit → elastic limit → yield → ultimate → break.
Hooke's law valid up to limit of proportionality.
Ductile: mild steel; brittle: cast iron (no yield point).
Fatigue = repeated load; creep = slow flow when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hooke's law: within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain.

why.en: Atoms behave like tiny springs for small stretches.

recall_q.en: State Hooke's law.

explain_simple.en: Pull twice as hard, it stretches twice as much.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Young's modulus E = tensile (or compressive) stress / linear strain. Steel E ≈ 200 GPa (2 × 10⁵ N/mm²).

why.en: It measures stiffness in pulling or pushing.

recall_q.en: Young's modulus of steel?

explain_simple.en: Big E = hard to stretch.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Modulus of rigidity G (shear modulus) = shear stress / shear strain. Steel G ≈ 80 GPa.

why.en: It measures stiffness against twisting and shearing.

recall_q.en: Shear stress ÷ shear strain = ?

explain_simple.en: How hard it is to twist.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bulk modulus K = direct stress (equal on all sides) / volumetric strain.

why.en: It measures stiffness against squeezing from all sides.

recall_q.en: Bulk modulus = ?

explain_simple.en: How hard it is to squeeze smaller.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Relations: E = 2G(1 + μ) and E = 3K(1 − 2μ).

why.en: The elastic constants are linked through Poisson's ratio.

recall_q.en: Relation between E, G and μ?

explain_simple.en: Know two constants, find the rest.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Combined relation: E = 9KG / (3K + G).

why.en: Eliminating μ from the two relations gives this.

recall_q.en: E in terms of K and G?

explain_simple.en: Another way to link the three moduli.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Elongation of a bar: δL = P L / (A E).

why.en: From E = σ/ε, with σ = P/A and ε = δL/L.

recall_q.en: Formula for change in length of a bar under axial load?

explain_simple.en: More load or length → more stretch. More area or E → less stretch.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Principle of superposition: total effect of many loads = sum of effects of each load acting alone (within elastic limit).

why.en: In the elastic range, effects add up in a straight line.

recall_q.en: Principle used to add effects of several loads on a bar?

explain_simple.en: Work out each load separately, then add.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bar of varying (stepped) section: total δL = (P/E)(L₁/A₁ + L₂/A₂ + ...).

why.en: Each part stretches by its own amount; add them.

recall_q.en: How is total elongation of a stepped bar found?

recall_a.en: Add elongations of each part: Σ PL/(AE).

explain_simple.en: Stretch of each piece, added together.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Uniformly tapering circular bar: δL = 4PL / (π E d₁ d₂).

why.en: Area changes steadily from d₁ to d₂.

recall_q.en: Elongation of a tapering circular bar?

explain_simple.en: Like a normal bar, but using both end diameters.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Elongation of a bar due to its own weight = w L² / (2E) = W L / (2AE).

why.en: Each section carries only the weight below it, so the average is half.

recall_q.en: Elongation of a bar due to self-weight is what fraction of an equal end load?

explain_simple.en: Own weight stretches it half as much as the same load at the end.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Composite section: two materials joined to share a load. Both have the same strain; loads add: P = P₁ + P₂.

why.en: They are fixed together, so they stretch equally.

example.en: Reinforced concrete column (steel + concrete).

recall_q.en: In a composite bar under load, what is the same for both materials?

explain_simple.en: Joined parts stretch together and share the load.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In a composite bar, σ₁/E₁ = σ₂/E₂. The stiffer material carries more stress.

why.en: Equal strain means stress is proportional to E.

recall_q.en: Modular ratio m = ?

explain_simple.en: The stiffer part takes more of the load.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections

points.en: E = σ/ε; G = τ/φ; K = σ/εv.
δL = PL/AE; stepped bar: add parts.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Metals expand when heated and shrink when cooled.

why.en: Heat makes atoms vibrate more and need more room.

example.en: Gaps are left between rail lengths.

recall_q.en: What happens to a metal rod when heated?

explain_simple.en: Hot metal grows; cold metal shrinks.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Free expansion δL = α L ΔT. α = coefficient of linear expansion (per °C).

why.en: Expansion depends on length, material and temperature rise.

example.en: Steel α ≈ 12 × 10⁻⁶ /°C.

recall_q.en: Formula for thermal expansion?

explain_simple.en: Longer bar or more heat → more growth.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: If expansion is prevented, thermal stress is set up: σ = E α ΔT.

why.en: The supports push back by exactly the amount it wanted to grow.

recall_q.en: Thermal stress in a fully restrained bar?

explain_simple.en: Stop it growing and stress builds up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermal stress does not depend on the length or area of the bar.

why.en: Length cancels in σ = E × (αLΔT / L).

recall_q.en: Does thermal stress depend on bar length?

explain_simple.en: Short or long, same thermal stress.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Heated and restrained → compressive stress. Cooled and restrained → tensile stress.

why.en: Heated bar tries to grow but is pushed back; cooled bar tries to shrink but is held.

recall_q.en: A restrained bar is heated. What stress develops?

explain_simple.en: Heated + blocked = squeezed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: If supports yield by δ, thermal stress σ = E (αLΔT − δ) / L.

why.en: Part of the expansion is allowed, so less stress builds up.

recall_q.en: If supports allow some movement, does thermal stress rise or fall?

explain_simple.en: A little room reduces stress.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Composite bar heated: material with higher α goes into compression; lower α goes into tension.

why.en: They must expand the same amount, so the faster one is held back.

example.en: Copper (higher α) and steel bars joined: copper in compression, steel in tension.

recall_q.en: Copper and steel bars joined and heated. Which is in compression?

explain_simple.en: The one that wants to grow more gets squeezed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In a composite bar with temperature change, compressive force in one = tensile force in the other.

why.en: No outside load, so internal forces balance.

recall_q.en: In a heated composite bar, how do the forces in the two parts compare?

explain_simple.en: One pushes, one pulls, by the same amount.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coefficient of linear expansion: aluminium ≈ 23, copper ≈ 17, steel ≈ 12 (all × 10⁻⁶ /°C).

why.en: Aluminium grows almost twice as much as steel.

example.en: Aluminium pistons need more clearance than cast iron ones.

recall_q.en: Which expands more: aluminium or steel?

explain_simple.en: Aluminium grows fastest with heat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Area expansion coefficient β ≈ 2α. Volume expansion coefficient γ ≈ 3α.

why.en: Area grows in two directions, volume in three.

recall_q.en: Volume expansion coefficient in terms of α?

explain_simple.en: Volume grows three times as fast as length.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Shrink fit: a part is heated to expand, fitted on a shaft, and grips tightly as it cools.

why.en: Thermal contraction creates a strong press.

example.en: Flywheel ring gear and steel tyres on rail wheels are shrink fitted.

recall_q.en: How is a starter ring gear fitted on a flywheel?

explain_simple.en: Heat it, slip it on, let it cool and grip.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A steel rail is fixed at both ends. Temperature rises by 40°C. E = 2 × 10⁵ N/mm², α = 12 × 10⁻⁶ /°C. Find stress.

explain.en: Heated and held, so compressive.

recall_q.en: Is the stress in a heated fixed rail tensile or compressive?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Restrained: σ = EαΔT, independent of length.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Friction is the force that resists sliding between two surfaces in contact. It acts opposite to motion.

why.en: Tiny bumps on the surfaces catch on each other.

example.en: Brakes and clutches work by friction; tyres grip the road by friction.

recall_q.en: Direction of friction force?

recall_a.en: Opposite to motion (or tendency of motion).

explain_simple.en: Friction holds things back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Static friction acts before motion starts. Dynamic (kinetic) friction acts during motion. Static friction is greater.

why.en: It takes more force to start sliding than to keep sliding.

example.en: Pushing a stalled car is hardest at the start.

recall_q.en: Which is greater: static or kinetic friction?

explain_simple.en: Starting is harder than keeping going.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Limiting friction is the maximum static friction just before sliding begins.

why.en: Any more force and the body starts to slide.

recall_q.en: Maximum friction just before motion is called?

explain_simple.en: The last grip before slipping.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction.

why.en: A rolling wheel does not rub along the surface.

example.en: That is why vehicles have wheels and ball bearings are used.

recall_q.en: Which is smaller: rolling or sliding friction?

explain_simple.en: Rolling is easier than dragging.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coefficient of friction μ = F / R (friction force / normal reaction). It has no unit.

why.en: It tells how slippery or grippy two surfaces are.

example.en: Dry tyre on dry road μ ≈ 0.7–0.8; on wet road much less.

recall_q.en: Coefficient of friction formula?

explain_simple.en: Friction force ÷ pressing force.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Laws of dry friction: friction ∝ normal reaction; it does not depend on contact area; it depends on the nature of surfaces; it acts opposite to motion.

why.en: These are Coulomb's laws of friction.

recall_q.en: Does friction depend on area of contact?

explain_simple.en: Push harder, more friction; bigger area, same friction.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Kinetic friction is almost independent of speed at low speeds.

why.en: This is another law of dynamic friction.

recall_q.en: Does sliding friction change much with speed?

recall_a.en: No — nearly constant at low speed.

explain_simple.en: Slow or a bit faster, friction stays about the same.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Angle of friction φ: tan φ = μ. Angle of repose: the steepest slope on which a body rests without sliding. Angle of repose = angle of friction.

why.en: On that slope, the weight's sliding part equals limiting friction.

recall_q.en: Relation between angle of repose and angle of friction?

explain_simple.en: The steepest slope before it slides.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fluid (viscous) friction occurs between layers of a fluid or between lubricated surfaces. It is much smaller than dry friction.

why.en: An oil film separates the metal surfaces.

recall_q.en: Friction between well-lubricated surfaces is called?

explain_simple.en: Oil makes surfaces slide on a liquid film.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Boundary friction happens when the oil film is very thin, as at engine start-up.

why.en: Surfaces partly touch, so wear is highest.

recall_q.en: When is engine wear highest?

explain_simple.en: At start, oil has not reached everywhere yet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Force to pull a body up a rough slope P = W (sin α + μ cos α), with P parallel to the slope.

why.en: Pull must beat both gravity along the slope and friction.

recall_q.en: Force needed to move a body up an inclined plane (force along plane)?

explain_simple.en: Fight gravity plus friction.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Friction is useful in brakes, clutches, belts, tyres, nuts and bolts, and walking. It is harmful in bearings, pistons and gears.

why.en: It wastes energy as heat and causes wear.

recall_q.en: Give one useful and one harmful case of friction.

explain_simple.en: Good for stopping, bad for moving parts.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Angle of repose = angle of friction, tan φ = μ.
Fluid friction lowest; wear highest at start-up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Centre of gravity (CG) is the point where the whole weight of a body seems to act.

why.en: We can treat all the weight as one force at that point.

recall_q.en: Point where the total weight of a body acts?

explain_simple.en: The balance point.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Centroid is the geometric centre of a plane area. For a uniform body, centroid and CG are the same point.

why.en: Areas have no weight, so we use 'centroid'.

recall_q.en: Centre of a plane area is called?

explain_simple.en: Centroid = middle of a shape.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Centroid of a triangle is at h/3 from the base. Of a semicircle: 4r/(3π) from the diameter.

why.en: More area is near the base, so the centroid is low.

recall_q.en: Centroid of a triangle from its base?

explain_simple.en: One-third of the height up from the base.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A vehicle with a low CG is more stable and less likely to overturn.

why.en: Higher CG gives a bigger tipping moment on turns.

example.en: Overloading luggage on a bus roof raises CG and risks rollover.

recall_q.en: Is a low or high CG better for vehicle stability?

explain_simple.en: Low and wide = stable.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Moment of inertia (second moment of area) shows how an area is spread around an axis. Unit: mm⁴ (area), kg·m² (mass).

why.en: More area far from the axis = stiffer beam.

recall_q.en: Unit of area moment of inertia?

explain_simple.en: How far the material is spread from the centre line.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MI of a rectangle about its centroid axis: I = b d³ / 12. About its base: b d³ / 3.

why.en: Depth d is cubed, so deep sections are much stiffer.

recall_q.en: MI of a rectangle about its centroidal axis?

explain_simple.en: Depth counts much more than width.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MI of a circle about its diameter: I = π d⁴ / 64. Polar MI: J = π d⁴ / 32.

why.en: Polar MI is twice the diametral MI.

recall_q.en: MI of a circular section about its diameter?

explain_simple.en: Circle: πd⁴/64; polar: πd⁴/32.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MI of a triangle about its base = b h³ / 12; about its centroidal axis = b h³ / 36.

why.en: Centroid axis is closer to the area, so smaller MI.

recall_q.en: MI of a triangle about its centroidal axis?

explain_simple.en: Triangle: /12 at base, /36 at centroid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Parallel axis theorem: I = Ig + A h². Perpendicular axis theorem: Iz = Ix + Iy (for plane areas).

why.en: These let us shift or combine axes.

recall_q.en: State the parallel axis theorem.

explain_simple.en: MI about a shifted axis = own MI + area × distance².

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Radius of gyration k = √(I / A). It is the distance at which all area could be packed to give the same MI.

why.en: Used in column and flywheel calculations.

recall_q.en: Formula for radius of gyration?

explain_simple.en: A single distance that represents the spread.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: I-sections are used for beams and chassis frames because most material is far from the neutral axis, giving high MI for low weight.

why.en: Flanges carry most bending stress; the thin web joins them.

recall_q.en: Why are I-sections used as beams?

recall_a.en: High MI (stiffness) with less material and weight.

explain_simple.en: Material placed where it works hardest.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Centre of gravity and moment of inertia

points.en: CG = balance point; centroid = centre of area.
Rectangle I = bd³/12; circle πd⁴/64; polar πd⁴/32.
Parallel axis: I = Ig + Ah²; k = √(I/A).

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A beam is a horizontal member that carries loads at right angles to its length and bends.

why.en: Loads across its length cause bending, not just stretching.

example.en: Vehicle axles and chassis side members act as beams.

recall_q.en: What is a beam?

recall_a.en: A member carrying transverse loads, which bends.

explain_simple.en: A bar that bends under load placed across it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cantilever beam: fixed at one end, free at the other.

why.en: The fixed end holds both force and moment.

example.en: A balcony slab, a diving board.

recall_q.en: A beam fixed at one end and free at the other?

explain_simple.en: Stuck in the wall at one end only.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Simply supported beam: rests freely on supports at both ends.

why.en: Supports give only upward reactions, no moment.

example.en: A plank across a drain.

recall_q.en: Beam resting freely on two end supports?

explain_simple.en: Sits on two supports, not fixed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Other beams: overhanging (extends past a support), fixed (both ends fixed), continuous (more than two supports), propped cantilever.

why.en: Support type decides reactions and bending.

recall_q.en: Beam with more than two supports?

explain_simple.en: Count supports and see how ends are held.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Point load: acts at a single point. Uniformly distributed load (UDL): spread evenly along a length, in N/m.

why.en: Total UDL = w × length, acting at the middle of that length.

example.en: UDL: a beam's own weight. Point load: a person standing at one spot.

recall_q.en: Unit of UDL?

explain_simple.en: Point = one spot. UDL = spread evenly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Shear force at a section = algebraic sum of vertical forces on one side of it.

why.en: It tells how much the section tends to slide.

recall_q.en: Shear force at a section is the sum of what?

recall_a.en: All vertical forces on one side of the section.

explain_simple.en: Add up the up and down forces to one side.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bending moment at a section = algebraic sum of moments of forces on one side about that section.

why.en: It tells how much the beam tends to bend there.

recall_q.en: Bending moment at a section = ?

recall_a.en: Sum of moments of forces on one side about the section.

explain_simple.en: Forces × distances to one side.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bending moment is maximum where shear force is zero or changes sign.

why.en: dM/dx = F, so M peaks when F = 0.

recall_q.en: Where is bending moment maximum?

recall_a.en: Where shear force is zero (changes sign).

explain_simple.en: Look for zero shear to find biggest bending.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cantilever with point load W at free end: max SF = W, max BM = W L at the fixed end.

why.en: The load acts over the whole length to the support.

recall_q.en: Max bending moment of a cantilever with end load W?

explain_simple.en: Load × length, at the wall.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cantilever with UDL w over length L: max SF = wL, max BM = wL²/2 at the fixed end.

why.en: Total load wL acts at L/2.

recall_q.en: Max BM of a cantilever with UDL?

explain_simple.en: Total load × half the length.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Simply supported beam with central point load W: reactions W/2 each, max BM = WL/4 at the centre.

recall_q.en: Max BM of a simply supported beam with central load W?

explain_simple.en: Middle load → WL/4 at the middle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Simply supported beam with UDL w: reactions wL/2, max BM = wL²/8 at the centre.

why.en: Shear is zero at mid-span, so BM peaks there.

recall_q.en: Max BM of a simply supported beam with UDL?

explain_simple.en: UDL on simple beam → wL²/8.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: SFD shape: point loads give horizontal steps; UDL gives a sloping straight line. BMD: point loads give straight lines; UDL gives a parabola.

why.en: Each integration raises the curve's degree by one.

recall_q.en: Shape of BMD under UDL?

explain_simple.en: UDL: SF sloping line, BM curve.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sagging BM (beam bends like a smile, concave up) is positive. Hogging BM (like a frown) is negative.

why.en: This is the usual sign convention.

example.en: Simply supported beam sags; cantilever hogs.

recall_q.en: Bending like a smile is called?

explain_simple.en: Smile = sagging. Frown = hogging.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Point of contraflexure: where bending moment changes sign (becomes zero).

why.en: The beam changes from sagging to hogging there.

example.en: Found in overhanging beams.

recall_q.en: Point where BM changes sign is called?

explain_simple.en: Where the bend flips direction.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bending equation: M/I = σ/y = E/R.

why.en: It links bending moment, stress, distance from neutral axis and curvature.

recall_q.en: Write the bending equation.

explain_simple.en: Bending stress = M × y / I.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Neutral axis: the line in a bent beam with zero stress. Above it is compression, below it tension (for sagging).

why.en: Top fibres shorten, bottom fibres lengthen; the middle stays the same.

recall_q.en: Stress at the neutral axis?

explain_simple.en: The middle line is neither pushed nor pulled.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Section modulus Z = I / y_max. Max bending stress σ = M / Z. Rectangle: Z = b d² / 6.

why.en: Bigger Z means stronger beam in bending.

recall_q.en: Section modulus of a rectangle?

explain_simple.en: Bigger Z = stronger beam.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Max deflection: cantilever end load WL³/3EI; simply supported central load WL³/48EI; simply supported UDL 5wL⁴/384EI.

why.en: These standard results are asked directly.

recall_q.en: Max deflection of a simply supported beam with central load?

explain_simple.en: Learn the three standard deflection formulas.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Torsion equation: T/J = τ/r = Gθ/L.

why.en: Used for shafts like propeller shafts and axles under twisting.

recall_q.en: Write the torsion equation.

explain_simple.en: Twisting a shaft: torque, stress and twist angle linked.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A hollow shaft is stronger and stiffer than a solid shaft of the same weight.

why.en: Material far from the centre resists twisting best.

example.en: Propeller shafts are hollow tubes.

recall_q.en: Why are propeller shafts hollow?

explain_simple.en: Hollow tubes twist less for their weight.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A 4 m simply supported beam carries a 10 kN load at the centre. Find reactions and max BM.
Reactions: each support takes half = 5 kN.

explain.en: Load is in the middle, so it is shared equally.

text.en: It occurs at the centre, under the load.

summary.en: Max BM = WL/4 at the centre.

recall_q.en: Max BM for 10 kN at centre of a 4 m simple beam?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A 2 m cantilever carries a UDL of 3 kN/m. Find max SF and max BM.
Max SF = 6 kN at the fixed end.
Max BM = wL²/2 = 3 × 4 / 2 = 6 kN·m at the fixed end.

summary.en: Cantilever UDL: SF = wL, BM = wL²/2.
Both are largest at the fixed end.

recall_q.en: Where are SF and BM largest in a cantilever?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Beams, shear force and bending moment

points.en: Cantilever: WL (point), wL²/2 (UDL) at fixed end.
Max BM where SF = 0; contraflexure where BM = 0.
UDL: SFD straight slope, BMD parabola.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A rivet is a permanent fastener: a round rod with a head, put through holes in plates, and the other end hammered into a second head.

why.en: Riveted joints cannot be opened without breaking the rivet.

example.en: Old truck chassis frames and bus bodies use rivets.

recall_q.en: Is a riveted joint permanent or temporary?

explain_simple.en: A metal pin squashed at both ends.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Parts of a rivet: head, shank (body) and tail (point).

why.en: The tail is formed into a second head after fitting.

recall_q.en: The cylindrical body of a rivet is called?

explain_simple.en: Head, body, tail.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rivet head types: snap (cup/button), pan, countersunk, conical. Countersunk heads sit flush with the surface.

why.en: Flush heads are used where a smooth surface is needed.

recall_q.en: Which rivet head sits flush with the plate?

explain_simple.en: Countersunk = flat, hidden head.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lap joint: one plate overlaps the other and they are riveted together.

why.en: Simple to make, but the load path is offset.

recall_q.en: Joint where one plate overlaps another?

explain_simple.en: Plates laid one over the other.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Butt joint: plates meet end to end and are joined by one or two cover (strap) plates.

why.en: Load stays in line, so it is stronger than a lap joint.

recall_q.en: In a butt joint, how are the plates connected?

explain_simple.en: Ends touch; a patch plate joins them.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Single riveted: one row of rivets. Double riveted: two rows. Arrangement can be chain (in line) or zig-zag (staggered).

why.en: More rows carry more load.

recall_q.en: Rivets in staggered rows are called?

explain_simple.en: Chain = rivets in line. Zig-zag = rivets staggered.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pitch (p) is the distance between centres of adjacent rivets in a row. Margin is the distance from rivet centre to plate edge (about 1.5d).

why.en: Too small a margin tears the plate edge.

recall_q.en: Distance between centres of adjacent rivets in a row?

explain_simple.en: Pitch = gap between rivets.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Back pitch is the distance between rows. Diagonal pitch is the distance between rivets in adjacent rows in zig-zag riveting.

why.en: Row spacing affects joint strength.

recall_q.en: Distance between two rows of rivets?

explain_simple.en: Back pitch = row-to-row gap.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ways a riveted joint can fail: shearing of rivets, tearing of plate between rivets, crushing of rivets or plate, tearing of plate at the edge.

why.en: Design checks each one; the weakest decides strength.

recall_q.en: Name two failures of a riveted joint.

recall_a.en: Rivet shearing, plate tearing, crushing, edge tearing.

explain_simple.en: Rivet cuts, plate rips, or parts get crushed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tearing strength of plate per pitch length: Pt = (p − d) t σt.

why.en: The hole removes metal, so only (p − d) is left.

recall_q.en: Tearing resistance of plate per pitch?

explain_simple.en: Metal left between holes × thickness × stress.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Shearing strength of a rivet in single shear: Ps = (π/4) d² τ. In double shear: Ps = 2 × (π/4) d² τ (theoretically).

why.en: In double shear the rivet is cut at two places.

recall_q.en: Shearing strength of a rivet in single shear?

explain_simple.en: Rivet area × shear stress.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crushing strength: Pc = d × t × σc (per rivet).

why.en: Projected area of the rivet against the plate = d × t.

recall_q.en: Crushing strength of a rivet?

explain_simple.en: Diameter × thickness × crushing stress.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Strength of the riveted joint = the least of tearing, shearing and crushing strengths.

why.en: The joint fails at its weakest point.

recall_q.en: Strength of a riveted joint equals?

recall_a.en: The least of Pt, Ps and Pc.

explain_simple.en: A chain is as strong as its weakest link.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Efficiency of a riveted joint = least strength / strength of the solid plate (p × t × σt).

why.en: Holes always weaken the plate, so efficiency is below 100%.

recall_q.en: Efficiency of a riveted joint formula?

recall_a.en: Least of (Pt, Ps, Pc) ÷ (p t σt).

explain_simple.en: How strong the joint is compared with uncut plate.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Unwin's formula gives rivet diameter: d = 6√t (mm), when t > 8 mm.

why.en: Thicker plates need thicker rivets.

recall_q.en: Unwin's formula for rivet diameter?

explain_simple.en: Rivet size from plate thickness.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Caulking and fullering make riveted joints leak-proof, as in boilers. Fullering is the better method.

why.en: Plate edges are hammered tight to seal gaps.

recall_q.en: Methods to make riveted boiler joints leak-proof?

explain_simple.en: Hammer the edges to seal.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rivets are commonly made of mild steel, wrought iron, copper or aluminium.

why.en: Rivet material must be ductile to form a head.

recall_q.en: Main property needed in a rivet material?

explain_simple.en: Soft enough to hammer a head.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pop (blind) rivets are fixed from one side only, using a rivet gun.

why.en: Useful where the back of the joint cannot be reached.

example.en: Used in vehicle body panels and number plates.

recall_q.en: Rivet fitted from one side only?

explain_simple.en: A rivet you fit with access from one side.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Rivet: head, shank, tail; permanent joint.
Lap joint vs butt joint (cover plates); chain vs zig-zag.
Failures: shearing, tearing, crushing, edge tearing.
Joint strength = least; efficiency = least / ptσt.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A bolt is a threaded rod with a head, used with a nut. It is a temporary (removable) fastener.

why.en: Parts can be taken apart for repair.

recall_q.en: Is a bolted joint permanent or removable?

explain_simple.en: Bolts can be undone; rivets cannot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Types: through bolt (with nut), tap bolt (screwed into a threaded hole), stud (threaded both ends), cap screw, set screw.

why.en: Each suits a different fitting job.

example.en: Cylinder head is fixed with studs or head bolts.

recall_q.en: A rod threaded at both ends with no head is called?

explain_simple.en: Stud = double-ended thread.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bolt heads: hexagonal (most common), square, eye bolt (for lifting), T-bolt, hook bolt, foundation bolt.

why.en: Hexagon heads fit standard spanners.

recall_q.en: Which bolt is used for lifting heavy parts?

explain_simple.en: Eye bolt has a ring to lift with.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Locking devices stop nuts loosening from vibration: lock nut, split pin with castle nut, spring washer, Nyloc nut, tab washer.

why.en: Vehicles vibrate constantly.

example.en: Steering linkages use castle nuts with split pins.

recall_q.en: Locking device used with a castle nut?

explain_simple.en: Extra parts stop nuts shaking loose.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pitch of a thread is the distance between two adjacent threads. Lead is the distance moved in one turn. Single start: lead = pitch.

why.en: Multi-start threads move faster per turn.

recall_q.en: For a single-start thread, lead equals?

explain_simple.en: Pitch = thread spacing. Lead = travel per turn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thread forms: V-thread (fastening), square and acme (power screws like jacks), buttress (one-way heavy loads).

why.en: Square threads have less friction and transmit power well.

recall_q.en: Which thread form is used in screw jacks?

explain_simple.en: V for holding, square for lifting.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Core (root) diameter is the smallest diameter of a thread. Stress in a bolt is calculated on the core area.

why.en: That is the weakest section.

recall_q.en: Bolt stress is calculated on which diameter?

explain_simple.en: Use the thinnest part of the thread.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A spring is an elastic part that bends under load and returns to its shape when the load is removed.

why.en: It absorbs shocks, stores energy and keeps parts pressed together.

example.en: Suspension springs, valve springs, clutch springs.

recall_q.en: Give one use of springs in a vehicle.

explain_simple.en: A spring gives way and springs back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Types of springs: helical (compression, tension), leaf (laminated), torsion, spiral (flat coil), disc (Belleville).

why.en: Each shape suits a different load.

example.en: Leaf springs in trucks; coil springs in cars; diaphragm (disc) in clutches.

recall_q.en: Laminated springs are also called?

explain_simple.en: Coil, leaf, twist, spiral, disc.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spring index C = D / d (mean coil diameter ÷ wire diameter). Usual range 4–12.

why.en: Too low is hard to make; too high buckles.

recall_q.en: Formula for spring index?

explain_simple.en: How fat the coil is compared with the wire.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stiffness (spring rate) k = load / deflection (N/mm).

why.en: It tells how hard the spring is to compress.

recall_q.en: Formula for spring stiffness?

explain_simple.en: Force needed for 1 mm squeeze.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Deflection of a close-coiled helical spring: δ = 64 W R³ n / (G d⁴) = 8 W D³ n / (G d⁴).

why.en: The wire twists, so G (rigidity) is used.

recall_q.en: Which modulus is used for close-coiled helical spring deflection?

explain_simple.en: Coil springs work by twisting the wire.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Springs in series: 1/k = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂ (softer). Springs in parallel: k = k₁ + k₂ (stiffer).

why.en: Series shares deflection; parallel shares load.

recall_q.en: Two springs in parallel: total stiffness?

explain_simple.en: Side by side = stiffer. One after another = softer.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Solid length is the length of a compression spring when coils touch each other.

why.en: The spring cannot compress further.

recall_q.en: Length of a spring when all coils touch?

explain_simple.en: Squeezed fully flat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leaf spring: longest leaf is the master leaf, with eyes at both ends. The spring is held to the axle with U-bolts and a centre bolt.

why.en: Master leaf connects the spring to the frame.

recall_q.en: Top longest leaf of a leaf spring is called?

explain_simple.en: The master leaf has the eyes at its ends.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spring materials: high-carbon steel, silicon-manganese steel (leaf springs), chrome-vanadium steel (valve springs).

why.en: They need high elastic limit and fatigue strength.

recall_q.en: Common steel for leaf springs?

explain_simple.en: Springs need tough, springy steel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wahl's factor corrects shear stress in helical springs for wire curvature and direct shear.

why.en: Inner side of the coil has extra stress.

recall_q.en: Factor that corrects helical spring stress for curvature?

explain_simple.en: An extra multiplier for coil springs.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spring surge: vibration of valve spring coils at high engine speed, so the valve does not follow the cam.

why.en: Coil resonance matches the cam frequency.

example.en: Fixed by double valve springs or variable pitch springs.

recall_q.en: Why are double valve springs used?

recall_a.en: To prevent spring surge and valve float.

explain_simple.en: Two springs stop wild bouncing at high rpm.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Bolt, stud, tap bolt, set screw; locking: split pin, lock nut.
Square thread for jacks; core diameter for stress.
Spring index C = D/d; stiffness k = W/δ.
Leaf spring: master leaf, U-bolt; double valve springs stop surge.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Welding joins metals permanently by melting and fusing them, with or without filler metal.

why.en: The joined metal becomes one piece.

example.en: Bus body frames and chassis repairs are welded.

recall_q.en: Is a welded joint permanent?

explain_simple.en: Melt and join the metal together.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Butt weld: plates placed edge to edge in the same plane and welded. Fillet weld: plates at an angle (lap or T) welded at the corner.

why.en: Fillet welds have a triangular cross-section.

recall_q.en: Weld with a triangular cross-section joining lapped plates?

explain_simple.en: Butt = edge to edge. Fillet = in the corner.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Butt weld edge preparations: square, single-V, double-V, single-U, double-U, J.

why.en: Thick plates need bevelled edges so weld metal reaches the full depth.

recall_q.en: Name one edge preparation for a butt weld.

explain_simple.en: Shape the edges so weld fills the whole thickness.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fillet weld types: transverse (load at right angles to weld) and parallel (load along the weld). Transverse is stronger.

why.en: The load spreads differently.

recall_q.en: Which fillet weld is stronger: transverse or parallel?

explain_simple.en: Weld across the load is stronger.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Weld terms: leg (size s), throat (t), root, toe, face, reinforcement.

why.en: Strength is calculated on the throat.

recall_q.en: On which dimension is fillet weld strength calculated?

explain_simple.en: The throat is the weakest line through the weld.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Throat thickness of a fillet weld t = 0.707 × leg size s.

why.en: For a 45° fillet, throat = s × sin 45°.

recall_q.en: Throat thickness of a fillet weld?

explain_simple.en: About 7/10 of the leg.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Strength of a parallel fillet weld P = 0.707 s l τ (per weld). Transverse: P = 0.707 s l σt.

why.en: Throat area × allowable stress.

recall_q.en: Strength of a parallel fillet weld?

explain_simple.en: Throat area × shear stress.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Strength of a butt weld P = t × l × σt (t = plate thickness, l = weld length).

why.en: The full plate thickness is welded.

recall_q.en: Strength of a butt weld in tension?

explain_simple.en: Thickness × length × stress.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Welding types: gas (oxy-acetylene), arc (MMAW/stick, MIG, TIG), resistance (spot, seam), and solid-state (friction).

why.en: Each uses a different heat source.

example.en: Car body panels are spot welded.

recall_q.en: Car bodies are mainly joined by which welding?

explain_simple.en: Gas flame, electric arc or electric resistance.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oxy-acetylene flame is about 3200°C. Neutral flame (equal O₂ and C₂H₂) is used for most welding.

why.en: Too much oxygen (oxidising) or gas (carburising) changes the metal.

recall_q.en: Temperature of an oxy-acetylene flame?

explain_simple.en: The hottest gas flame used for welding.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MIG uses a consumable wire electrode with shielding gas. TIG uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode.

why.en: TIG gives cleaner, precise welds, used for aluminium and stainless steel.

recall_q.en: Which welding uses a tungsten electrode?

explain_simple.en: MIG feeds wire; TIG uses tungsten.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Welded joints vs riveted: welded are lighter, leak-proof, faster and 100% efficient possible; but need skill and may have residual stresses.

why.en: No holes weaken the plate in welding.

recall_q.en: Give one advantage of welded over riveted joints.

explain_simple.en: Welding: no holes, less weight.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Welding defects: porosity, slag inclusion, lack of fusion, incomplete penetration, undercut, cracks.

why.en: Each weakens the joint.

recall_q.en: Gas holes in a weld are called?

explain_simple.en: Bubbles, dirt and gaps make weak welds.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brazing and soldering join metals without melting the base metal. Soldering filler melts below 450°C; brazing above 450°C.

why.en: Only the filler melts.

example.en: Radiator cores are soldered or brazed.

recall_q.en: Which joins with filler melting below 450°C: soldering or brazing?

explain_simple.en: Soldering is low-heat, brazing is higher heat; base metal stays solid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Butt weld edge-to-edge; fillet weld in the corner.
Fillet strength = 0.707 s l τ; butt = t l σt.

explain.en: Pascal's law: pressure in a confined fluid is passed equally in all directions.
